articleTitle: Improving Drone Operational Efficiency through IoT-Blockchain Integration
abstract: This article presented a new hybrid modular framework incorporating IoT technologies and blockchain. One of the proposed framework’s main goals is to eliminate the flaws related to drone communication networks, including security risks and performance inefficiency. The article reveals the examination that helps drone operations become more secure, efficient, and reliable using the alternate framework. There is tremendous progress, which is visible when you compare it to ordinary communication methods. These are the significant findings from the experiment in which 120 milliseconds were reduced to 90 milliseconds of transmitting time. Also, from 50 Mbps to 70 Mbps, the amount of data sent each second is improved, and the operational time improved from 95% to 99%. Besides, integrated mechanisms also increase and reach up to 95% of the initial 70% of the capability of fighting cyber-attacks. However, it offers perfect data integrity at the whooping rate of 100%. This directs blockchain technology as the pillar of drone communications because it provides safe access and secures communications from unauthorized tampering. Moreover, the 5 Wh of energy saved from 40 Wh to 35 Wh suggests that the framework is the most efficient while solving the need for sustainability and the effectiveness of drone operations. Moreover, these achievements reveal the framework’s superiority in resolving drone communication systems’ challenges and, ultimately, fuel the evolution of drone technology used in various sectors by providing a reliable and flexible system.

articleTitle: End-to-End SNR Capacity and throughput enhancement Using Non-Orthogonal Multiple access and Massive MIMO in 5G
abstract: This study provides a detailed analysis of the potential improvements in 5G network performance due to the adoption of NOMA and Massive MIMO technologies. Obtaining higher data rates, reduced latency, and increased overall network capacities remain a primary objective, and the research provides a comparison based on simulated data. Simulation models are designed to compare the proposed model against the conventional implementation of 5G networks based on a set of primary indicators, namely, throughput and latency. An abstract Wave Efficiency indicator is also presented to showcase a new metric for determining the qualitative improvements in signal processing and spectrum utilization. As the results of the research have demonstrated, the incorporation of NOMA and Massive MIMO increases overall network throughput while reducing latency. This demonstrates the potential contributions of these technologies to making wireless communications systems more efficient and reliable. The introduction of the Wave Efficiency is offered as a measurable variable for displaying the qualitative improvement in the wireless communications technologies, facilitating further implementation of NOMA and Massive MIMO in 5G networks.

articleTitle: An Efficient Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning for Blockchain Network
abstract: Blockchain innovation has as of late drawn in a great deal of interest as a potential major advantage for various applications. By the by, there are as yet significant snags with blockchain organizations’ presentation and versatility. AI approaches give possible solutions to improving and advancing blockchain network activities around here. There is an additional opportunity for supporting the proficiency of blockchain networks: choice tree calculations. These calculations are prestigious for being basic, interpretable, and adaptable. This study dives into choice tree-based AI procedures that are planned in light of blockchain networks. We go over the hypothesis behind choice trees and how they work comparable to blockchain innovation. We likewise give a careful survey of the writing on blockchain network issues settled by choice tree calculations, including pertinent exploration, strategies, and contextual investigations. We trust that by doing this examination, we will show how choice tree AI approaches might work on the proficiency, security, and adaptability of blockchain networks.

articleTitle: Crop Yield Prediction
abstract: The negative effects of climate change has been attributed to the significant decrease in crop performance that India’s agricultural industry has seen over the past 20 years. Before harvest, accurate crop yield forecast is necessary for enable farmers and governments to make well informed decisions on marketing and storage tactics. The aim of this initiative is to enable farmers to produce the greatest decisions possible by giving them a trustworthy tool for pre-planting crop yield estimation. To address this difficulty, the creation of a working prototype for an interactive prediction system is essential. The objective is to offer farmers with the necessary knowledge to predict crop yields efficiently by utilizing diverse data analytics techniques and crop prediction algorithms. The key to overcoming this difficulty is creating a working interactive prediction system prototype. The goal is to give farmers the information they need to properly predict their crop yields by utilizing an assortment of data analytics techniques and crop prediction-specific algorithms. Crop production forecasting relies heavily on the random forest algorithm’s implementation.

articleTitle: Development and Optimization of Simulation Model of Decision Aid System Implementation
abstract: The use of simulation modeling of production activities to improve the effectiveness of management decisions allows to evaluate the quality of the decision made on the model, as well as a means of training employees. The relevance of the research topic in the management of the project to create a decision support system (DAS) using simulation modeling is that in today’s world more and more organizations face the need to make decisions based on the analysis of large amounts of data and information. For this purpose, it is necessary to use special tools and methods that will allow to process data quickly and accurately and make decisions based on the results obtained.

articleTitle: Optimized VGG16 Model for Advanced Classification of Cotton Leaf Diseases
abstract: The cotton leaf disease infliction anywhere puts the production of agricultural products at risk as well as sustainable farming causing both problems and solutions of the meaningless disease detection. In this research, we propose an optimized Visual Geometry Group (VGG) 16 model for the advanced classification of four major cotton leaf diseases: leaf curl, bacterial blighty, leaf spot, and wilt. Integration of deep learning methods, transfer learning as well and other approaches is what the model focuses on to raise the disease detection accuracy rate and realize the management of agriculture precision. And, there was a complete dataset, which included images of cotton plants from infected leaves with various diseases. This dataset was annotated properly and preprocessed. VGG16 model was pre-trained with a substantial data set of ImageNet image database and then fine-tuned to perform the cotton leaf disease classification task using existing transfer learning techniques. The achieved model efficacy has been evaluated using commonly accepted evaluation metrics. These include accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Results show that the invented technique performs well when the revised VGG 16 model obtains satisfactory accuracy and disease-related metrics when applied to all three disease categories. The level of comparative analysis with current best models justifies done method efficacy and its strength in cotton leaf disease classification. This study’s findings have an essential consequence on precision farming. It grants farmers a scalable solution relevant for the quick and automated monitoring, early diagnosis, and possibly treatment of plant diseases. Future investigation may rule in the superiority of applying the modified model to practical agricultural fields for ready accessibility and usability. Ultimately, these findings are moving us into the phase of development of agricultural informatics and offer evidence of the ability of deep learning to radically change approaches to fighting crop disease.

articleTitle: Email Spam Monitoring System
abstract: Emails are extremely important in business and other forms of communication, and they have been recognized as one of the most significant and extensively utilized forms of communication in contemporary times. They have evolved into a convenient means of disseminating information. Being on the Internet makes you vulnerable to attacks, and emails are no exception. And emails are more vulnerable as compared to other sources, as the user can be a victim of cyber-attacks like phishing, spamming, ransomware, malware injection, etc. using email. So, to detect and inspect such suspicious emails, we have develop an Email Monitoring System that will detect such emails based on defined parameters and convictions and on some suspicious keywords such as hijacking, explosion, etc. Attackers commonly use email phishing and spamming as they are the simplest methods to deceive someone and trick them into clicking on a malicious link through an email that appears authentic. These emails are used to breach a computer’s defense systems. The malicious links shared within the email are designed to mimic the spoofed organization by utilizing their logos and legitimate content. In this article, we will explain the distinguishing characteristics of fraudulent emails, why it is crucial to detect them, and how machine learning techniques and models with an alleged algorithm can be used to identify them within an email message.

articleTitle: Maximizing Privacy in Reinforcement Learning with Federated Approaches
abstract: Data protection issues and security in the age of technological advancement have become problematic, mainly because these methods are increasingly widespread. This paper covers critical problems of Federated Reinforcement Learning (FRL) and shows how this technique could provide a viable solution to the issue. We are attempting the use case scenario of the Federation Q-learning in the Labyrinth difficulties here. It ensures that technological requirements are adapted at all levels and keeps the information secret. A trial has been made to test the application of IRL on AI training, enabling the scientists to acquire actual proof of the advantages of FRL against the theoretical approaches in training, which are the majority. The main quantitative facet of this case uses pretty scientific statistics. Research results from conventional Q-learning and our variation, codel bean Q-learning, are significant in drawing conclusions and gaining insights. The federated q-learning presented scores around 25% higher than the q-learning with an agent, which is one more advantage than the q-learning using an agent. Just as Federated Q-learning obtains fast policy optimization by reducing convergence time by 2 5%, parallelism also brings about quicker and more effective exploration of the Q-table. Federated Q-learning is no exception to the general rule that this model has an advantage in ensuring data privacy, yielding an evident four-point improvement in the data privacy score. This shows that this technology quickly becomes a trusted ally and can anonymize data without compromising users’ privacy and security. Moreover, in the final stage of our work, the implementation of the model pretty soon caused an improvement in computer efficiency by 40%. The results showed that the current traditional AIL techniques suddenly faced five times more risks concerning privacy and security.

articleTitle: Breast Cancer Detection Using Nanoparticle Sensor with Machine Learning Algorithms
abstract: This research is mainly focused on the early detection of breast cancer in women by their urine samples with nanoparticle sensors. It detects certain enzymes and proteins that can be the main cause of cancer by machine learning algorithms, correlation analysis, and logical regression methods and created a web-based breast cancer prediction website using started nanoparticle urine analysis data, which contains the DNA barcode sequences that match with DNA of patient urine which is user friendly to use for every person. This study mainly focuses on non-invasive cancer. We analyze non-invasive cancer by using urine sample test data collected from the patients, utilizing advanced technology to access DNA signatures associated with breast cancer biomarkers. Our approach involves the barcode of nanoparticle sensors, which matches the urine samples. After the urine samples match, they are applied to the sensors, translated into digital data, and transmitted to a centralized system. Now, the centralized system collaborates with datasets derived from previous breast cancer cases. The algorithm now analyses the urine data and identifies the patterns. Then, it correlates with different stages of breast cancer.

articleTitle: Network Intrusion Detection System using Random Forest and Gradient Boosting Machines
abstract: The recent technological advancements not only astonish us but also demonstrates that if they are misapplied, they can pose a serious threat. A Network intrusion Detection system (NIDS) is presented in this paper which leverages the abilities of Random Forest and Extreme gradient boosting Machine (Xgbm) classifiers and harnesses the ensemble of both classifiers which enhances the accuracy of the system and brings out the best in both the classifiers. The system is trained using the UNSWNB15 dataset. Additionally, the system also employs the statistical and Recursive Feature Elimination for feature selection which enhances the model’s performance.

articleTitle: Deep Learning in the Detection of Chronic Kidney Disease
abstract: Kidney stones are the main kidney-related issue that has arisen in recent times. Small kidney stones are notoriously difficult to detect, thus this research—known as the Detection of Chronic Kidney Disease Using Deep Learning—helps identify kidney tumors and cysts in addition to stones in the kidney. The primary goal of this effort is to reduce time delays and boost accuracy while using less electricity. Two Deep Learning models derived from Machine Learning are included in the paper. Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Mobile Net are the two models. The study was able to examine the accuracy of these two models in addition to the outcomes.

articleTitle: Brain Tumor Detection with YOLOv8
abstract: Brain tumors are cancer causing cells which when developed inside a person’s brain can cause them life threatening challenges. The major objective of this study is to detect brain tumors in the early stages of the disease by using a deep learning algorithm, YOLO v8, in the hopes of increasing the survival rates of the patients. The dataset is acquired from kaggle which contains annotated MRI images of brain tumors that belong to either meningioma, glioma, no tumor and pituitary class. To optimize the training process, diverse sizes and optimizers are used. Through this extensive experimentation the findings are recorded. The findings highlight the importance of optimization strategies in deep learning-based analysis of medical images and demonstrate the capability of YOLO v8 as a robust tool for brain tumor detection.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Performance of Various NOMA Systems Based on User Count and Minimum Rate Demand
abstract: In wireless communication networks, non-orthogonal multiple access, or NOMA, is a multiple access technique used to boost spectrum efficiency and system capacity. It is a multiplexing procedure that consents several users to stake the similar frequency band simultaneously. According to the channel circumstances, users in NOMA are divided into stronger and weaker groups. The stronger users are given higher power, while the weaker users are given lower power. Within each NOMA cluster, a number of users employ successive interference cancellation (SIC) and superposition coding (SC) approaches. This results in better utilization of the available resources and higher data rates for the users. As a result, NOMA has become a viable multiple access method for next wireless networks. However, there are several issues (inter & intra user interference, channel estimation problem, user scheduling, power allocation issue) need to be addressed for performance estimation in NOMA. As a result, the effectiveness of NOMA has been assessed in this work by evaluating the effects of minimum rate demand ($R_{{min}}^{k}$) and user numbers on the likelihood of outages and power consumption. The performance measures have been estimated for Fully SC-SIC NOMA, FD-NOMA and FDMA with different multiplexed users and their minimum demand rate on each sub channel.

articleTitle: Understanding IoT-23 Dataset: A Benchmark for IoT Security Analysis
abstract: As the number of Internet of Things (IoT) devices rises, robust cybersecurity solutions are desperately needed to shield these interconnected systems from ever-evolving threats. This paper presents a novel approach to identifying attacks using machine learning (ML) techniques, using the IoT-23 dataset as an evaluation standard. The IoT-23 dataset offers a diverse collection of network traffic data collected from a range of IoT devices, facilitating the development and validation of intrusion detection systems (IDS) specifically tailored for IoT scenarios. This method includes preprocessing the raw data, identifying pertinent features, and training ML models such as Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB), and K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN). Performance evaluation uses key performance indicators (KPIs) including accuracy, recall, precision, and F1-score to assess how effective the recommended approach is. The findings demonstrate how ML may enhance the security design of IoT systems by offering a proactive means of thwarting emerging cyber threats and a means of alerting users to them. The accuracy of the RF model may reach up to 89 %, whereas other models, such as KNN and XGB, yielded results of 85 % and 88 %, respectively.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Enhanced Federated Learning: A New Paradigm for Secure Distributed Machine Learning
abstract: Merging blockchain technology into Federated Learning makes a novel approach to boost security, trust, and scalability, which are critical questions about the formation of distributed machine learning. This given industry study examines which obstacles are and possible ways of mitigating them to implement blockchain technology in such settings and attempts to solve the primary weakness of distributed learning exhibited. This is supported by our study concerning the experimental approach with an emphasis on security policy changes indicated by our results. We were able to find the risk sources $25 \%$ up, and we were able to prevent the everyday common data leaks and model poisoning risks. Also, the jump from 70 to 95 security scores shows that providers have significantly improved their cybersecurity. The integration process, however, brings along a computational overhead, which can be estimated from the $\mathbf{9 0 \%}$ performance reduction from which the system efficiency score alters from 90 to 75. The designed framework increases scaling-level issues and trust among people groups. Scalability ratings have been improved from 80 to 85. Trust metrics, however, are now $30 \%$ higher, which took the metrics from 60 to 90. These statistical data show clearly that in the pursuit of security and trust, tradeoffs may arise in the form of increased computational resources. The tut gives a good reason for using blockchain technology in the FL model. It provides a comprehensive description of both pros and cons. It proposes principles that can be followed in subsequent research to advance and strengthen the system’s resilience in conjunction with its operation. The research that is covered in this paper contributes a new framework to the volatile subject of safe and scalable machine learning. This framework is designed to elevate the trustworthiness and reliability of distributed learning systems.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence for Image Classification of Skin Diseases with Convolution Transformer
abstract: AI is in its most prominent times due to the progress made in achieving better results in advanced tasks, especially in the field of computer vision. These improvements of different types of layers and architectures in deep learning have provided benefits in all related fields. One such related field is healthcare industry where different types of data and records related to patients is collected and maintained, which is used to develop screening and early diagnosis algorithms for easing the detection process. Transformer are good at sequence related classification task. An image matrix can be considered as a collection of various small patches. Patches when arranged in a sequence are able to provide information of the collective image in a whole. For this reason, Convolution Transformer are proposed for image classification task for dermnet dataset. Few techniques such as transfer learning and image augmentation with mix-up are also utilized for increasing the validation accuracy and minimizing the over-fitting. In this study, a custom convolution Transformer is utilized for modeling the dermnet dataset for classification. The proposed model achieves a validation accuracy of $73.8 \%$.

articleTitle: Collaborative Filtering Based Module Recommendation To Boost Learners Achievement
abstract: In today’s world learners have access to a plethora of information in online learning platforms to hone their skills in different fields. Although a large number of choices may seem good, but it also leads to choice overload. Recommender systems (RS) can play a pivotal role in personalizing e-learning experiences by providing tailored content through various techniques. One commonly employed technique in such systems is collaborative filtering (CF). In this study, we utilize autoencoders within a CF framework to suggest course modules to learners. Our approach demonstrates superior performance in enhancing personalized learning experiences, addressing challenges posed by high-dimensional and sparse data. Empirical results confirm the effectiveness of our model, surpassing traditional methods like KNN, SVD, SVD++, and NMF in terms of accuracy. This research contributes to advancing e-learning recommendation systems, highlighting the potential of autoencoder-based collaborative filtering in optimizing learner engagement and performance.

articleTitle: Simulation of EV Battery and its Optimum Design Components
abstract: The increasing popularity of electric vehicles (EVs) as sustainable modes of transportation demands a comprehensive understanding of battery dynamics and optimal design components. A sophisticated framework is developed, encompassing diverse models for EV simulation, thermal analysis, and Battery Management System (BMS) control. A Li-ion battery pack model is developed, showcasing critical parameters such as current, voltage, and State of Charge (SOC). The study also explores the integration of Photovoltaic (PV) systems with multiple storage methodologies, realized through a robust MATLAB/Simulink mathematical model, which provides valuable insights and serving as a vital reference for refining and optimizing battery performance in the quest for sustainable transportation solutions.

articleTitle: Optimization Accuracy of Secured Cloud Systems Using Deep Learning Model
abstract: Cloud security is vital in attracting data security and privacy customers. The online attackers disrupt the use of the on-demand services provided by the cloud service providers for their clients. It is distributed in nature for resource sharing over the Internet. Thus, security has become the main agenda for cloud computing usage by cloud customers. As a result, the financial growth of cloud-based organizations is increasing gradually. The critical situation of cloud security is identifying the types of attacks and deciding how to defend such attacks to protect the cloud data from attackers. Numerous methodologies are reviewed to determine the robust security mechanisms for cloud security to protect against DoS or DDoS attacks (by malware attacks, MITM attacks, or other medium attacks). The ML concept has incorporated algorithm conceptions like deep neural networks and quantum neural networks to enhance prediction and protection accuracy. These proposed models not only help to reduce the attack level up to $100 \%$ but also increase the trust of cloud users with financial growth to cloud service providers (CSPs).

articleTitle: Asteroid Hazard Assessment: Optimizing ExtraTrees with RandomizedSearch CV and SHAP Explainable AI
abstract: Thisresearch addresses the crucial task of classifying asteroids as hazardous or non-hazardous for effective hazard assessment. Leveraging a dataset obtained from NASA via Kaggle, comprising 4687 rows and 30 columns, we employed various machine learning algorithms to discern the best-suited model. The ExtraTrees classifier emerged as the top performer with an initial accuracy of 96.6%. Notably, further optimization through Randomized Search Cross-Validation elevated the accuracy to 97%. Our study emphasizes the importance of algorithm selection and finetuning in achieving reliable asteroid classification. Motivated by the critical need for accurate hazard assessment, this research highlights the ExtraTree classifier as a robust solution, showcasing its potential in advancing our understanding and mitigation strategies for potential asteroid impacts.

articleTitle: Dynamic Modelling and PI Control Design for Bidirectional SEPIC/ZETA DC-DC Converter in Battery Applications
abstract: The effective management of energy flow is essential in modern power systems, especially when it comes to applications involving Battery Energy Storage System (BESS). The bidirectional SEPIC/ZETA DC-DC Converter offers a promising solution that enables battery charging and discharging operations between the battery and the grid or other power sources. In this work, we describe the simulation of a proposed Bidirectional DC-DC Converter employing a state-space circuit averaged modelling technique to determine the transfer function for managing the switching pulses of the converter via a PID controller in both SEPIC and ZETA modes. The tuning process for the controller leverages the classic Ziegler-Nichols technique. The converter utilizes a dual loop control strategy implemented in MATLAB/Simulink, for constant current charging and discharging of the battery in which outer voltage control loop as well as inner current control loop is involved. The functionality of the bidirectional power flow control system has been thoroughly examined using MATLAB/Simulink simulations, ensuring its efficacy during both battery charging and discharging phases across diverse conditions.

articleTitle: Emotify: An AI-Powered Emotion-Based Music Recommendation System
abstract: This paper presents a practical implementation of a music system based on speech emotion recognition. The proposed model will recommend live playlists based on the user’s emotion where the emotion is extracted from speech input and an AIdriven system generates music playlists as per the recognized emotion class. ConvNet is used to classify the emotion from the speech input, and K Means is used to cluster music together into playlists. The music is recommended such that the mood of the user is elevated.

articleTitle: Real World Deployment of Dual Branch MRC Enhanced by Adaptive Algorithms LMS and RLS in 5G Networks to Improve SNR and QoS
abstract: This research is aimed at understanding the performance benefits of the use of adaptive algorithms in dual-branch MRC systems as a solution for developing 5G networks. We developed controlled simulations to determine the performance influences of the algorithms in SNR, QoS, BER, and throughput under different network conditions. Our results indicate that the algorithms significantly reduce BER safe power divergence that improves the reliability and performance of the communication platform. The adaptive systems in addition reveal a significantly impressive ability to maintain a higher rate of throughput that is necessary in the current networks due to the increasing volume of data consumed by different users. In conclusion, therefore, this research has showed that adaptive MRC techniques might be a highly-viable option toward enabling the development of 5G technology, provided a suitable method for boosting performance during uncertain communications.

articleTitle: EfficientNet-B0-Based Classification of Pneumonic Lungs Using Chest X-Ray Dataset
abstract: In this research paper, the authors take a new angle: classify pneumonic lungs by utilizing up-to-date architecture such as EfficientNet-BO. Given a huge X-Ray dataset of real cases, the model is excellent at identifying pneumonia. The study aims to address a crucial need in the area of respiratory medicine-through development and application for clinical diagnosis of diseases of the lungs which are efficient, accurate and can be used on everyone. Its strong ability to learn is shown as the model demonstrates an awesome 99.50% training accuracy, checks itself out by verifying results with a validation accuracy of 92.20%, and sits tight under pressure during testing with an accuracy at 99.28%. As a matter of fact, these results serve to remind us that this model is excellent in accurately identifying normal and pneumonic lung conditions. This research not only enriches the growing literature on deep learning techniques in medical image analysis but also offers an extremely valuable tool for health care providers which can rapidly and precisely diagnose pneumonia. The method uses the EfficientNet-B0 architecture, known for its high performance in image classification. The model is built from a rich and diverse Chest X-Ray dataset, ensuring that it can be generalized to different patient populations and conditions of imaging. The study’s findings hold promise for improving diagnostic accuracy, lowering human error as well as ultimately transforming patient outcomes in the realm of pneumonia detection by means automated image classification.

articleTitle: Investigating the Effectiveness of Deep Learning and Machine Learning for Bangla Poems Genre Classification
abstract: Bangla Poems Genre Classification is crucial for understanding and preserving cultural heritage. In this paper, we employ both machine learning and deep learning approaches to classify Bangla poetry genres. Our study encompasses a range of models, including Multinomial Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Extreme Gradient Boosting, CNN, GRU, and BERT. Experimental results reveal that the Naive Bayes model achieves the highest accuracy of 77%, outperforming other models. Additionally, we present performance metrics for each model, providing a comprehensive evaluation. This research contributes to the advancement of regional language natural language processing and fosters a deeper understanding of Bangla poetry through computational analysis.

articleTitle: Canine Demodicosis Detection in Dogs using Deep Learning
abstract: Detecting canine diseases holds immense significance for timely and precise diagnosis, facilitating effective treatment and care. In this proposed system, canine disease detection is achieved using deep learning techniques such as CNN, focusing on normal images of dogs. The utilization of these images provides valuable insights into the dog’s condition and enables the identification of various diseases, including mange. Deep learning techniques are employed to automatically extract features from these normal images and classify them into different disease categories. Transfer learning is applied to leverage pre-trained models and enhance the performance of the disease detection system. The proposed methodology shows promising results with an accuracy of 97% in accurately detecting and classifying canine diseases, providing a valuable tool in diagnosing and treating dogs more effectively.

articleTitle: Enhancing Software Test Effort Estimation using Ensemble Learning Algorithms
abstract: In software engineering, accurate test effort prediction is critical to project schedule and resource efficiency. Conventional approaches, which depend on past performance or expert opinion, frequently fail to provide a reliable estimate of the testing effort. These approaches might offer some insight at first, but as project complexity rises, they become less scalable and more error-prone. This study explores the use of machine learning to improve the estimation of software test effort in response. This work intends to overcome the shortcomings of conventional methods and create more accurate and scalable solutions by utilising the power of machine learning algorithms. The goal of the research is to determine the best machine learning strategy for software test effort estimation through extensive testing and comparative analysis. The results of this study are compared using metrics such as RMSE, MSE, MAE, and R2 score, with Random Forest algorithm demonstrating superior performance over other algorithms.

articleTitle: Metagenomic Face: Applying Machine Learning to Facial Microbiome Data for Pattern Recognition and Disease Classification
abstract: This innovative study utilizes machine learning techniques to analyze facial microbiome data, drawing inspiration from the metaphorical representation of microbial information through facial features. Leveraging the Olivetti Faces dataset as a model for facial microbiome data, the research introduces the Metagenomic Face framework. This framework facilitates the translation of microbial information into facial features, enabling the application of machine learning algorithms such as Random Forests or Neural Networks for pattern recognition. The investigation focuses on identifying correlations between facial features and underlying microbial compositions, aiming to assess the feasibility of classifying health and disease states based on these patterns. Preliminary results demonstrate promising outcomes, with precision, recall, and accuracy metrics reaching 0.94, 0.91, and 0.91, respectively, and support for the model encompassing 80 instances. These findings underscore the potential of Metagenomic Face as an innovative approach to microbiome analysis, shedding light on the intricate relationship between facial features and microbial communities. Furthermore, a comparative analysis involving Support Vector Machine, Logistic Regression, and Random Forest classifiers reveals compelling performance metrics. The Support Vector Machine Classifier attained an accuracy rate of 85%, the Logistic Regression Classifier showed an accuracy of 91%, and the Random Forest Classifier displayed a matching accuracy of 91%. These additional insights contribute to a comprehensive understanding of the Metagenomic Face framework’s efficacy compared to alternative machine learning approaches, emphasizing its potential in advancing precision medicine through microbiome analysis.

articleTitle: Harmonic Harmony: Advancing Musical Instrument Classification through CNN-SVM
abstract: This research intends to improve the field of Music Information Retrieval (MIR) by creating and comparing a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Support Vector Machine (SVM) approaches for the precise identification of five distinct musical instruments. The process of categorizing is quite intricate because of the subtle timbre characteristics coming from the musical sounds. We have done a detailed study evaluation of the model. To evaluate each class of instrument, we have employed precision, recall, F1-score and accuracy metrics. The precision for the model in Class 1 was 89.5, the recall was 93.76, the F1 score was 91.58, and the accuracy was 97. articleTitle: Enhanced Medicinal Plant Identification: Leveraging Machine Learning and Image Processing for Accurate Raw Material Recognition
abstract: Data on medicinal plants and raw materials encompasses details about diverse botanical resources employed for their healing attributes in both traditional and contemporary medical practices. The difficulties in improving the identification of medicinal plants include fluctuations in image quality caused by elements such as lighting, background clutter, and camera angles, which affect the accuracy of algorithms, as well as the shortage of varied training data, potentially resulting in biases or inaccuracies during recognition. To address the challenges mentioned earlier, utilize customized Extended Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) techniques capable of managing variations in image quality and utilizing diverse training data to enhance the precision of medicinal plant identification. The Extended CNN approach provides better flexibility in handling varied image attributes and heightened precision in medicinal plant recognition, thanks to its specialized architecture and utilization of extensive training datasets.

Author Keywords: Image Quality Variability and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)

articleTitle: Enhancing Health Monitoring in Academic Institutions of Bangladesh: Assessing Annual Checkups and the Role of Digital Health System
abstract: Despite the early adoption of school-based annual health checkups in developed countries like Japan over a century ago, many developing nations, including Bangladesh, lag behind in implementing such practices. This absence hampers preventive healthcare efforts crucial for disease prevention. This research delves into the current landscape of annual health checkups in Bangladeshi academic institutions through a survey involving 94 university students. Alarmingly, $74.47 \%$ of respondents reported a lack of exposure to health checkups. This deficiency extends to families, exacerbating the prevalence of diseases like diabetes. Additionally, limited awareness of the importance of annual health screenings results in significant healthcare expenditures. To address these challenges, this study proposes the adoption of a digital health system to bolster primary healthcare delivery and facilitate costeffective health monitoring, particularly in resource-constrained settings.

articleTitle: 4-Way Ka-Band Power Combiner Using Rectangular Waveguide
abstract: The design and analysis of a 4:1 WR28 waveguide power combiner developed for Ka-band frequency microwaves has been presented and designed using the electromagnetic simulation platform, CST Studio Suite. Within the specified 32 to 38 GHz frequency range, this proposed power combiner works seamlessly with Ka-band systems. Combining rigorous electromagnetic simulation with optimization techniques, the design achieves combining gain of 5.5 dB, high isolation, good return loss and impedance matching. The combiner was simulated in high-frequency problem type and the assigned material was silver. The VSWR is obtained between 1 and 2 making it ideal for a combiner to combine waves with minimum reflection and return loss is obtained below - 10 dB. Experimental validation further highlights the suitability of the designed power combiner for practical deployment in Ka-band systems.

articleTitle: Analysis of Workload in Google Cluster Trace based on Job Termination Events
abstract: One of the major problems facing cloud service providers is cloud failure since the behavioral features of cloud loads in data centers are not directly visible. Characterizing the Google Trace has many benefits, including improving system performance by failure prediction, resource efficiency, and task scheduling algorithms. Enhancing our knowledge of task behavior in the termination state of jobs in compute clouds is the aim of our effort. In this work, we examine and analyze the unique behavior of tasks related to terminated jobs using a Google Cluster Trace. We seek to establish a correlation, statistical, and distribution analysis of all task occurrences in each event of terminated jobs separately. Based on our findings to improve the dependability of cloud-based apps, the failure and terminated prediction systems can take advantage of job resource usage trends and their characterization.

articleTitle: Offensive Language Identification in Dravidian Codemixed Dataset
abstract: This research uses an English-Malayalam dataset taken from YouTube comments to investigate improper language detection in multilingual settings. To capture the subtleties of language usage—such as code-mixing—that are common in the under-resourced Dravidian language family, we use autoencoders and ensemble techniques using BERT models as features. We use LIME in addition to improve interpretability. A lazy classifier that uses a variety of classifiers also helps to determine which classifier is the most efficient. Supervised learning methods are enhanced by unsupervised k-means clustering. Our results surpass standards and demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in offensive language identification. The field’s understanding is advanced by this confluence of methodologies.

articleTitle: Prediction of Ayurveda Herbs and its Benefits using CNN and MobileNet Algorithms in Deep Learning
abstract: Ayurveda has been an integral part of ancient Indian medicine and it still plays an important role in the creation of Homeopathic medicines. In this paper we have introduced a comprehensive system for detecting, grading, and classifying Ayurveda Herbs by taking images as input and analyzing those images using two Deep Learning Algorithms CNN and MobileNet. The proposed system employs advanced technology to accurately identify different categories and classes of Ayurvedic Herbs, utilizing image processing and machine learning techniques for classification and gradation using Deep Learning Algorithms like CNN and MobileNet. Additionally, it stores a pre-trained uses and benefits data for each and every Ayurvedic Herbs Class and displays the information based on the class of Ayurveda Herbs detected.

articleTitle: Agricultural Informatics: Assessing CNN and Decision Tree Effectiveness in Indian French Bean Variety Classification
abstract: This study delves into the application of CNNs and DT to classify prominent French bean varieties in India, including Selection-9, Pusa Parvati, and Arka Suvidha. A vast assortment of almost eight thousand carefully chosen high-resolution photos illustrating different stages of development, lighting arrangements, and viewpoints. The study’s overarching goal is to create a reliable classification system that can autonomously extract meaningful information from photos using CNN and visually distinguish between different varieties of beans using DT. With an overall accuracy of 98.7 percent, the model proved it was expert at correctly classifying the three French bean kinds according to their outward look. measures like accuracy, recall, and F1 score were used to evaluate the model’s performance. These measures revealed the model’s strengths for each group. Specifically, they shed light on its ability to classify different items. On top of that, the Misclassifications were exposed by the Confusion Matrix. The results of this investigation showed where the model could use some improvements. By developing a computational tool for the accurate classification of numerous French bean varieties, this work improves agricultural practices. Farmers, researchers, and anybody else involved in the worldwide distribution of crops greatly benefit from this procedure of supplying accurate information about the type and origin of crops. By doing so, we can be sure that everyone taking part in this crucial endeavor has all the information they need to make educated choices. Negative outcomes may result from neglecting this task. As a result, you must participate in and back this initiative, which is called Give Something Back (GSB). This lays the groundwork for future innovations in crop differentiation and shows how effective it is to use advanced educational strategies to improve agricultural operations. Future work can concentrate on improving the model’s performance in a wider range of environmental scenarios and increasing the amount of data collected.

articleTitle: Mining Comments and Sentiments in YouTube Live Chat Data
abstract: The proliferation of social media and internet usage has led to an exponential growth in data volume and dynamic user interactions. Within this digital landscape, YouTube Live Chat analysis has emerged as a compelling area for understanding spontaneous user engagement. Central to this analysis is sentiment analysis, which extracts opinions and sentiments, offering valuable insights for content creators and industries seeking to understand user perspectives. This paper presents a thorough examination of mining comments and sentiments within the dynamic environment of YouTube Live Chat data. Our study involves analyzing the live chat of YouTube live streams, applying sentiment analysis to the live feed, and presenting a real-time dashboard to streamers. By leveraging sentiment analysis, including the interpretation of emojis, we aim to offer content creators and platform administrators valuable insights into audience reactions, opinions, and sentiments. Our system enables users to access real-time sentiment analysis of live chat interactions, facilitating the delivery of more engaging content. Ultimately, our goal is to equip content creators, platform administrators, and researchers with actionable insights into audience engagement, preferences, and emotional resonance within the digital realm.

articleTitle: Exploring Socioeconomic Influences on Life Expectancy through Machine Learning Ensemble Regression Techniques
abstract: Life expectancy prediction is a critical area in public health research, aiding in policy formulation and resource allocation. In this study, we explored the prediction of life expectancy using a dataset sourced from Kaggle. Initially, the dataset underwent rigorous preprocessing to handle missing values and ensure data quality. Subsequently, a diverse array of regression models, including Multiple Linear Regression (MLR), SVM, Gradient Boosting, Random Forest, XGBoost, and Decision Tree were applied to the dataset. Through thorough evaluation, the top-performing models were identified, and a comparative analysis was conducted. Leveraging ensemble learning techniques, specifically stacking and voting ensemble, further refinement was achieved, resulting in a robust predictive model with high R-squared values. The results highlight the effectiveness of ensemble regression methods in forecasting life expectancy, offering valuable insights for public health policy and decision-making.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis of Indian Tourist Place Reviews: A Machine Learning-Based Exploration
abstract: the social media trend, where many followers are interested in visiting the areas based on the reviews offered by the influencers, has caused the tourism industry to start growing incredibly high in recent years. This study conducts sentiment analysis on user-generated reviews from online tourism review websites, employing advanced feature extraction techniques. The dataset which has been taken from different web sources contains textual reviews and numerical ratings, providing the framework for analysis. Data preprocessing includes text tokenization, stop word removal, lemmatization, and data cleaning, resulting in a refined dataset with a processed review column. For feature extraction, we used TF-IDF vectorization (limited to 5000 features) and GloVe-based word embedding for enhancing word importance and semantic relationships. We employ different machine learning models such as Naive Bayes, SVM, Logistic regression, and Random Forest Classifier (with 100 decision trees) for sentiment analysis, which is designed to handle complex data relationships. Random Forest has given the best accuracy of 89.54 percent compared to the other models, while future work will encompass precision, recall, and F1-score. Our novel approach integrates TF-IDF, word embedding, and Random Forest for improved sentiment analysis. This methodology results of subsequent discussion by a robust foundation for further exploration in this field.

articleTitle: Implementation of Neural Network using Posit Arithmetic Circuits
abstract: The recent upsurge in interest regarding Neural Networks has resulted in the development of increasingly intricate networks that place a heavy demand on computational and memory resources. These networks consist of numerous interconnected processing units, with each unit conducting computations involving weighted sums and the assessment of an activation function. Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) can be optimized for high speed, low power, and small area usage with various techniques. DNNs can also tolerate small errors resulting from approximate arithmetic operations to some extent, but the extent of this tolerance depends on factors like network architecture and precision. Striking a balance between approximation and maintaining acceptable accuracy is crucial when applying these optimizations for resource-constrained or efficient DNN deployments. The proposed neural network architecture leverages parallel memory access and rapid, approximate Multiply-Accumulate Computations (MAC) units in the fully connected layers. Initially, in this paper, a floating-point MAC unit is designed, which includes an IEEE-754 floating-point multiplier and adder/subtractor unit of 32-bit width. However, due to the compelling advantages of posits over floating-point numbers, such as a broader dynamic range, enhanced accuracy, consistent bitwise results across systems, simplified hardware and streamlined exception handling, a Posit Arithmetic Unit (PAU) generator capable of producing 32-bit width PAU adders and multipliers is subsequently developed. The primary objective is to demonstrate that the PAU generator surpasses a floating-point MAC unit in terms of accuracy and speed for implementing a neuron within a neural network.

articleTitle: OpenCV-enabled Gesture Control for Smart Devices: A User-Centric Approach
abstract: This research delves into the realm of human-computer-interaction, presenting an innovative user-centric approach togesture control for smart devices. Integrating the powerful OpenCV (Open-Source Computer Vision Library), our system demonstrates enhanced accuracy, responsiveness, and user satisfaction in real-world scenarios. The study includes a comprehensive evaluation of the system’s performance, addressing identified limitations, proposing improvement strategies, and exploring potential applications in emerging technologies. By analyzing a diverse dataset and employing a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), our OpenCV-enabled gesture control system showcases its adaptability to varied gestures and environmental conditions. Future directions include addressing limitations, expanding application scopes, and integrating with emerging technologies, positioning this research at the forefront of advancements in gesture recognition technology.

articleTitle: Personalized Skincare Product Recommendation System Using Content-Based Machine Learning
abstract: Beyond the limitations of conventional methods, the growing demand for skincare products has created a need for more individualized recommendations. This paper presents a novel method for creating a machine learning-based skincare product recommendation system using content-based filtering. The system provides customized recommendations by examining the chemical makeup of products and taking individual skin types into account. By entering their preferred beauty impacts, users can improve the system’s ability to adjust to their preferences. The implementation of user interface design, product composition assessment methodology, and content-based filtering are described. The system’s ability to provide tailored recommendations is demonstrated by empirical evidence, and it holds great promise for transforming consumer experiences in the cosmetics industry.

articleTitle: Performance of Microstrip Notch Antenna in RF Energy Harvesting for 2.45 Ghz Wi-Fi Applications
abstract: This Paper shows the design and simulation of a micro strip notch with an inset feed antenna. This antenna is suitable for the Wi-Fi band and has also shown the Return loss, gain and VSWR Parameter, which has been analyzed in this work. The tiny size, cost-effectiveness, simplicity of production, and omnidirectional emission pattern make this antenna appealing. We have used the CST Studio suite software to design and simulate the proposed antenna.

articleTitle: Detecting Car Speed using Object Detection and Depth Estimation: A Deep Learning Framework
abstract: Road accidents are quite common in almost every part of the world, and, in the majority, fatal accidents are attributed to over speeding of vehicles. The tendency to over speeding is usually tried to be controlled using check points at various parts of the road but not all traffic police have the device to check speed with existing speed estimating devices such as LIDAR based, or Radar based guns. The current project tries to address the issue of vehicle speed estimation with handheld devices such as mobile phones or wearable cameras with network connection to estimate the speed using deep learning frameworks.

articleTitle: Channel Modeling for Free Space Optical Communication Using Generative Adhversarial Network
abstract: Fast data transfer speeds are offered via Free Space Optical (FSO) communications, which have applications in a variety of industries. Still, a significant obstacle to improving the performance of the FSO system is accurate channel modeling. In this paper, a novel approach to channel modeling in FSO communications using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) is presented. By learning the complex mapping between broadcast and received signals, a class of deep learning models known as GANs is utilized to generate realistic channel representations. The proposed method leverages the generating and discriminative capabilities of GANs to capture the intricate characteristics of FSO channels, including air turbulence effects and beam divergence. Our suggested approach, which makes use of GANs, provides an innovative and efficient FSO channel modeling solution that surpasses traditional analytical and empirical methods. We demonstrate the potential of our GAN-based approach to enhance FSO system design and performance optimization in real-world applications by demonstrating its better performance in precisely modeling FSO channels through rigorous testing and evaluation.

articleTitle: Data Enhancement Strategy Using Reinforcement Learning And Xgboost With BlockChain Security
abstract: The enormous volumes of data generated by Next Generation Sequencing (NGS) technology have transformed genomics and made efficient data analysis techniques necessary. To create data analytics applications, the extraction, transformation, and loading (ETL) process is necessary. In understanding data features, representation, storage, I/O operations, intermediate findings, in-memory analysis, and total processing time, the data format is crucial, as this study emphasizes. Data conformance is required for effective analysis since different machine learning and data mining algorithms require different types and forms of data. In this paper, we explore data format-centric optimization of the ETL process for NGS data analysis. We investigate how computing efficiency and analytical correctness are affected by the choice of data type. By using distributed computing and parallel processing, we evaluate the effectiveness of several data formats in NGS data analysis processes, such as FASTQ, BAM, and VCF. Our study offers suggestions for developing data analytics applications in the genomics field by clarifying the relationship between data format, ETL, and algorithmic needs. We also look at the trade-offs between resource usage and data format choice. In the end, our study contributes to more accurate and efficient genomics research by addressing the urgent need for well-informed data format options in NGS data analysis.

articleTitle: FPGA-Compatible Fog Rectification and Contrast Enhancement for Improved Vision Algorithms in Foggy Environments
abstract: abstract-Fog rectification is a crucial preprocessing step in enhancing image quality for applications like autonomous driving and object recognition, particularly in foggy and hazy conditions. This paper presents a streaming fixed-point implementation of a fog rectification and contrast enhancement algorithm tailored for FPGA deployment aiming to enhance visibility and contrast in foggy images. The fog rectification involves the dark channel of the image calculating the airlight map, refining it with filters and restoring the defogged image. Contrast enhancement is achieved through RGB to gray conversion and contrast stretching. The proposed algorithm is designed to efficiently process foggy RGB images, removing haze and enhancing contrast. The implementation utilizes fixed-point blocks from Vision HDL Toolbox for FPGA compatibility and employs a streaming pixel format for real-time processing. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the algorithm in improving image quality for vision algorithms in foggy environments.

articleTitle: AgriFusion: Crop Recommendation System using Ensemble Learning Methods
abstract: Agriculture is vital for human survival, heavily influenced by climate and soil. Picking up the most suitable crop at the perfect time gives the best crop yield. To help the farmers in the decision-making process a recommendation system is built by considering the parameters of a crop like temperature, climate, location, relative humidity, type of soil, soil pH, and other factors using ensemble learning algorithms and data analysis techniques. A user-friendly interface is designed for hassle-free usage of the recommendation system by the farmers along with a hint of yield prediction. Algorithms like SVM, logistic regression, Naïve Bayes, Decision trees, random forest, gradient boosting, and other ensemble methods are used to train the model and based on their performance the model is used for the recommendation system. This helps leverage the decision-making of the farmers for the crop type.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a Low Phase Noise Oscillator using Substrate Integrated Waveguide without Metallic Vias
abstract: This research paper presents the design and analysis of a low phase noise oscillator operating at 4.9 GHz utilizing an Improved Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) with modifications involving metallic vias. The oscillator’s performance is evaluated based on its S-parameters, with a focus on achieving superior impedance matching, signal transmission, and stability. The chosen frequency of operation aligns with various applications in wireless communication, radar systems, satellite communication, industrial automation, scientific research, and medical devices. The oscillator design exhibits an S11 reflection coefficient of -22.9 dB and an S21 transmission coefficient of -5.606 dB, indicating efficient power transfer and satisfactory signal transmission characteristics. These parameters reflect the oscillator’s ability to maintain impedance matching while minimizing insertion loss, crucial for ensuring optimal performance in diverse applications. The paper discusses the significance of the 4.9 GHz frequency range in various real-world applications and justifies its selection based on operational requirements and industry standards. The proposed oscillator design aims to address the growing demand for reliable, low phase noise oscillators in modern communication systems and other technological domains. Through detailed analysis and simulation results, this research demonstrates the viability and effectiveness of the proposed oscillator design, contributing to advancing the field of microwave oscillator design and offering insights into optimizing phase noise performance, stability, and efficiency in SIW-based oscillator circuits with modified metallic vias.

articleTitle: AI-Enhanced Lung Cancer Detection Using the ResNext50 Architecture
abstract: Lung cancer as the first cause of cancer death among people in many countries shows the necessity of creating a straightforward as well as accurate test for identifying the disease at an early stage. In the last several years automatic learning (AI) of machine learning (ML) technologies have been regarded as great techniques for medical diagnostics with the help of imaging analysis. This article will take the ResNext50 architecture, a variant of convolutional neural networks (CNN), as a model. It will use the ResNext50 architecture as an example of the AI-enhanced lung cancer detection neural network. The methodology has the following steps: obtain a versatile database of CT scans (chest) with labeled cancerous lung lesions. As preprocessing steps, we apply techniques like normalization, resizing, and augmentation for standardization, and the augmentation for enhancement of the dataset. ResNext50 is embraced as the main backbone for the lung cancer detection system being an advantage of transfer learning and fine-tuning, which helps improve the model’s efficiency. We assess the performance of the model according to a set of metrics which estimate the correctness of the model. These include accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, F1-score, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic (AUC-ROC) curve. Competitive evaluations are executed to compare the baseline methods and the superiority of the considered procedure. The results confirm that the ResNext 50 model reached a high level of 92%, with an accurate evaluation of metrics that matter. Performance check of the ResNext50 model versus baseline methods proves this model’s superiority and bringing out more significant advantages while working with advanced CNNs is recommended for lung cancer detection.

articleTitle: Fractional Order Controller for Stability Analysis of Hybrid Industrial Microgrid
abstract: Frequency stability is challenged by the growing incorporation of renewable energy sources in hybrid industrial microgrids, which lowers overall rotational inertia. The purpose of this research is to study how to improve frequency stability in such systems by using fractional sliding mode control. A precise mathematical model of the hybrid microgrid is created, taking into account different distributed generators, loads, and energy storage devices. An FSMC law introduces a fractional-order sliding surface in order to control frequency deviations. Comparing fractional order sliding mode control to standard integer-order sliding mode control, greater control degrees of freedom may result in faster and more reliable performance. This study demonstrates that the controller can keep the system stable even in the face of unforeseen and operational disruptions In this work, performance assessment is examined. The robustness of the FSMC to uncertainties in reaction time, settling time, and system parameter is evaluated by simulations. The frequency stability of hybrid industrial microgrids is improved by FSMC. In order to develop strong control strategies for these renewable energy systems, this work makes use of modeling, stability analysis, performance evaluation, and optimization.

articleTitle: Supercapacitor Assisted PV Powered Dynamic Wireless Power Charging System for EV
abstract: In electric vehicle(EV), the battery range plays an important parameter of efficiency and performance. The dynamic wireless power transfer (DWPT) based battery charging generally improves the range of the battery. In general, it becomes difficult to get the power from grid thorough the roadway. In this work, PV battery system is used as a main source in the transmitter side. In DWPT, the coupling coefficient and mutual inductance continuously changes, as a result the output voltage also fluctuates. Due to the fluctuation, the life cycle of battery may be reduced. In this work, a power management algorithm is proposed to optimize the power on the receiver side such that a constant voltage and desired current can be maintained on the battery of receiver side. To obtain that a super-capacitor (SC) is used as an auxiliary source on the receiver side. The SC will store the energy during high coupling between transmitter and receiver coil and discharges during weak coupling. The buck converter with a PI controller on the secondary side is to maintain desired charging current of battery. The simulation study is carried of ANSYS/ SIMPLORER and SIMULINK.

articleTitle: Breaking Boundaries: Harnessing the Power of Deep Learning Model Design to Predict Diabetes with Artificial Intelligence Assisted Prediction Strategy
abstract: Predicting the onset of diabetes at an early stage might greatly mitigate the disease’s devastating effects; the condition is currently incurable and results from chronically elevated blood sugar levels. Predicting the onset of diabetes has been the focus of current efforts within the deep learning community, building on decades of prior study. Nowadays, diabetes is a common and unfortunately incurable health problem. People can’t give their health the attention it needs because of their busy schedules. The food we eat is broken down into glucose, which is then released into our bloodstream. When blood sugar levels are too high, the pancreas secretes a hormone called insulin. A key function of insulin is to facilitate the uptake of glucose by cells for energy production. Identifying diabetes at an early stage can greatly improve the chances of leading a sustainable life. A fruitful way would be to use machine learning algorithms, which can improve themselves with future predictions after being taught and tested with massive amounts of data. This study presents AI-based Diabetes Prediction (AIDP), a model that explores diabetes data to make better predictions about the illness, with the severity of the condition in mind. The suggested rationale is tested against the traditional K-Nearest Neighbor (kNN) learning paradigm to see how well it works. Results from the planned study demonstrate that the model can accurately forecast the onset of diabetes, if not better. When compared to another deep learning method known as kNN, our results reveal that the suggested AIDP attained superior accuracy.

articleTitle: Plant Disease Detection Using Machine Learning
abstract: Plant diseases are a serious threat toworld agriculture, resulting in lower agricultural yields and financial losses. This study examines how machine learning methods could revolutionize the identification of plant diseases. The shortcomings of conventional approaches and suggest combining machine learning models with cutting-edge imaging and data processing technologies to improve the diagnosis’s speed and precision. This research demonstrates how well machine learning methods, such as CNN and SVM, can distinguish between healthy and unhealthy plants. Also gone through how transfer learning can be used, especially when data is scarce, to modify previously trained models for illness detection.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Double-Sided LCC Compensation Topology
abstract: EV charging is being revolutionized by Wireless Power Transfer (WPT). Compared to conventional wired methods, WPT offers significant advantages like improved safety, effortless operation, and the potential for extended charging ranges for mobile EVs. For the design of WPT, supply (grid) circuits, coupling system (consisting of both compensation & coil assembly) circuits, and EV batteries are very essential. One crucial element in enhancing the WPT system’s performance is the compensation circuit design. To charge EV batteries, this study uses the Inductor-Capacitor-Capacitor (LCC) compensation topology on both sides. Double-sided LCC (DS LCC) has characteristics: independence from coupling coefficient variations and load fluctuations in terms of resonant frequency. This translates to a more robust and adaptable charging system. This paper investigates the performance analysis of a DS LCC compensation network. The design and simulation of this system were conducted using Ansys Twin Builder software. This WPT system delivering 500 W of power at a frequency of 85 kHz using smaller additional inductors gives greater than 90 % efficiency in power transfer from source to load.

articleTitle: VGGAE-Net: A Two Stream Ensemble CNN for Diabetes Retinopathy Classification
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy is a retinal disease that leads to vision impairment in people suffering from diabetes mellitus. Early detection of disease requires expert supervision and computer diagnosis systems to avoid vision loss. Diabetic Retinopathy grading is suffering from small lesions and data imbalance problems. In this work, we proposed a VGG based attentive ensemble Network (VGGAE-Net) for the classification of diabetes Retinopathy. We have also utilized the two attention blocks channel attention module and class attention module with extracted feature maps from the CNN. Then their prediction outputs are combined to provide the final output for the classification task. The experiment shows that the ensemble approach of two attention blocks with VGG model gives 96.66% accuracy as compared to the existing recent models.

articleTitle: U-NET based Camaouflaged Object Detection
abstract: Because of the complex relationships between the target object and its surroundings, Camouflaged Object detection (COD) presents a unique challenge that goes beyond traditional object identification tasks. In order to detect objects that have been disguised, this work uses a 2D U-Net architecture It highlights how well this architecture preserves fine-grained spatial features due to its unique encoder-decoder structure with neglect links. Known as the identification of deliberately hidden objects that mix in with their surroundings, the detection of camouflaged objects depends on semantic segmentation, which is an area in which U-Net performs exceptionally well. The model is trained using the MCS1K training dataset, and its performance is evaluated using the MCS1K testing dataset. The average accuracy of 70.14 percent that has been reported highlights how effective the suggested method is at handling the complex problem of hidden object recognition.

articleTitle: Windows Forensic Analysis and Detection of Ransomware Attacks Using Event Logs and Tools
abstract: This paper explores the vital domain of cybersecurity, specifically focusing on the forensic analysis of Windows systems to detect and combat ransomware attacks. Through the meticulous examination of event logs and the utilization of specialized tools, the study presents a comprehensive approach to identifying ransomware incidents, understanding their modes of dissemination, and implementing effective mitigation strategies. By analyzing event logs and employing state-of-the-art forensic tools, the research uncovers the sophisticated tactics employed by ransomware perpetrators and identifies crucial patterns essential for timely detection and response. Furthermore, this study integrates practical insights with theoretical frameworks to provide actionable guidance for cybersecurity professionals, empowering them to strengthen Windows environments against the evolving ransomware threat landscape. Ultimately, this paper contributes to enhancing the resilience of organizations to ransomware attacks, safeguarding critical data and infrastructure against the pervasive menace of cyber threats.

articleTitle: Nine Level Quadra Boost Inverter with Modified Level Shifted Pulse Width Modulation Technique
abstract: This research initiatives to introduce a switched capacitor based nine level boost inverter (SC-9LBI) powered by modified level shifted pulse width modulation (PWM) technique. The SC-9LBI equipped with single DC source along with three capacitors and eight controlled switches to develop nine level inverter output voltage. The suggested inverter configuration has the ability of boosting the inverter input voltage into 1:4 ratio. Also, this research involves modified level shifted PWM technique to enhance the quality of inverter output voltage. The effectiveness of the NLMLI is assessed through parameters such as harmonic distortion, peak voltage, and output voltage root mean square value (rms). Simulation studies have been conducted using MATLAB/Simulink to evaluate the proposed inverter’s performance.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Based Auto-Grading Model for Question-Based Algebra Problems using RoBERTa
abstract: The use of Machine learning models into educational assessment has revolutionized the grading process for problemsolving domains.This research introduces a machine learning auto-grading model tailored for question-based algebra problems, utilizing RoBERTa, a natural language processing model.The primary objective is to investigate the adaptability of RoBERTa, originally designed for natural language understanding, for representing non-natural language mathematical expressions. The study also explores the impact of different embedding strategies on the performance of autograding systems for student responses to equation problems.The mathematical and textual code inputs were transformed into vectors, and the vectors were then fed into several models. Evaluation metrics such as RMSE, MSE, R2, and MAE are utilized to assess the effectiveness of each embedding approach in grading student responses accurately. The use of k-fold cross-validation will improve the dependability of the assessment measures, offering insights into the model’s consistency across different subsets of the data. The comparative analysis of different embedding strategies offers guidance on selecting the most suitable approach for enhancing the autograding process.

articleTitle: Design and Development of an IoT Enabled Low-Cost Smart Hand Glove System for Gait Detection in Stroke Patients
abstract: Stroke is a non-communicable disease in human beings signifies a critical, pervasive, and widely recognized health crisis. Stroke-induced gait alterations can significantly impact a patient’s ability to perform daily activities. In the recent past, stroke became one of the primary cause of the disability in elderly people and recorded as third leading cause of death globally. According to statistics given by National Center for Disease Informatics and Research(NCDIR), stroke is India’s 3rd leading source of death and the 6th leading reason of disability. To this end, there exists different rehabilitation models to detect human gait in stroke survivors. Human gait, a complex interplay of limb (arm or leg) movements, velocity, and energy cycles, holds crucial diagnostic information for stroke patients. Most of the existing models are cost effective and intrusive type, cause discomfort while using. Thus, in this paper, a wearable low-cost hand glove based system for gait detection and analysis for stroke survivors using IoT is proposed. The system leverages MEMS accelerometer sensor (ADXL335), offers a non-intrusive means of collecting gait dynamics like motion, shock or vibration and allows continuous monitoring. Further, the MEMS sensor is integrated into an IoT enabled hand glove with Wi-Fi communication module used for wireless monitoring of gait dynamics. Later, the collected data is analyzed using MATLAB. The analysis provides a thorough understanding of post-stroke gait patterns and cautions the stroke survivors about their abnormal gait. In addition, the proposed wearable hand glove model possibly saves the patients from future injuries and may allow to tailor rehabilitation strategies for every individual.

articleTitle: Adaptive Investment Strategies: Deep Reinforcement Learning Approaches for Portfolio Optimization
abstract: This paper addresses the role deep reinforcement learning (DRL) plays in portfolio management by making a timely and more accurate market prediction within the finance sector. Using these machines learning the methods, including the DRL algorithm, this program is designed to strengthen while making investment choices beyond the limits of the traditional framework, as well as enhancing the decision-making processes in an environment with many uncertainties and dynamics. The study begins with a literature review that is thorough and covers past works on traditional finance portfolio management, market prediction methods, and recent work on DRL in finance. Leveraging this base, we design and implement DRL-V-based models for asset management and market prediction situations. Empirical research includes the construction of models that use historical financial records about stock indexes and macroeconomic data as the main input. We use some of the performance metrics like cumulative returns, Sharpe ratio, maximum drawdown, and annualized volatility as the KPIs. We compare them with historical data along with the DRL model’s performance and other baseline models as well. The evidence obtained from the experiments proves that DRL-based investment strategies outperform other strategies by their ability to make adjustments for changing market standards and uncovering investment opportunities. Besides the comparative studies, the variety of DRL models used in DFS which perform similar tasks under different market environments has been validated.

articleTitle: Domain Specific Embeddings in RNN Frameworks for Hate Span Detection and Classification
abstract: The unrestricted use of the internet has led to a significant rise in the dissemination of hate speech online, posing serious threats of harm and violence to individuals and society at large. Social media data often comprises informal and fragmented sentences, interspersed with multiple languages. While numerous researchers are dedicated to identifying and mitigating hate speech in social media content, existing approaches primarily focus on detecting hate speech as a whole, rather than targeting specific hateful words or phrases. To encourage research in this direction, a shared task was formulated during SemEval 2021, a task called Toxic Span Identification, to detect hateful words present in a sentence. Leveraging the dataset provided by the organizers of the task, our approach entails constructing a model comprising three fundamental layers: feature extraction, a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) layer, and at last, a Conditional Random Field (CRF) layer. Among various embedding techniques, we found that GloVe embeddings yielded superior results with our base model, achieving an F1 score of ${6 1. 2 3 \%}$ when combined with dropout layer. Further Toxic BERT and HateBERT models were used to classify the comments as hateful or non-hateful, HateBERT outperformed the Toxic BERT model.

articleTitle: Advancing Named Entity Recognition with Gazetteer and Transformer-based language model for Hindi
