Although this virtual concept has made our day-to-day life easy and efficient with its multitenancy, shareability and metered usage; the fact that its implementation involves wired connectivity of servers, hard-drives and other network devices has created high power and energy consumption problems. Regular carbon emission from cloud data centers has largely increased the carbon footprint. One of the reasons for high energy consumption and power emission from these data centers is the elongated runtime as well as slow and flawed working algorithms. If we can decrease the runtime with some fast and efficient heuristic algorithm, the power consumption problem will be solved. Migrating the idle virtual machines to a Parking Server where they can stay idle and consume minimum resources can address the problem quite effectively. In this paper, I have presented such an algorithm in the name of Migration of Idle Machines via Parking Server Algorithm. This algorithm focuses on parking the idle virtual machines on an isolated parking server until that machine is assigned a task. The algorithm has shown great results and satisfactory accuracy.

articleTitle: Modelling and Analysis of Graphene based OLED
abstract: The primary focus of this paper is on modelling and analyzing organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs). These OLEDs are the most flexible in the market; they have a transparent electrode with graphene (a material with a thickness of 0.335 nm), exceptional brightness and outstanding flexibility, has a great deal of potential for enhancing OLED performance because of its unique characteristics, which include high mechanical flexibility, transparency, and electrical conductivity. The paper first addresses the current state of OLED technology before going into the potential benefits of employing graphene. In this work, the Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) method is employed to model the graphene layer on OLEDs. The far field intensity of various devices with graphene in OLED is analysed and results show that the intensity is more in comparison with conventional OLED.

articleTitle: Optimizing Renewable Energy Integration: A Hybrid Solar and Wind-Powered Smart Grid Enhanced with IoT Monitoring
abstract: Recognizing the constraints associated with fossil fuels, there has been a growing emphasis on elevating the adoption of renewable energy systems. However, there are a number of difficulties with the grid integration of renewable energy sources in terms of system performance, stability, reliability, and power quality. Solar photovoltaic (SPV) systems establish intermittent quantities of power. Therefore, it is essential to accurately predict the incoming solar energy and calculate the electricity, which is produced by SPV systems and electrical quality. In this paper, an IOT-enabled hybrid solar and wind energy-based smart grid is proposed. The Landsman converter is employed, which has a great voltage gain ratio for determining the PV system’s maximum output. Utilizing DFIG as MPPT (Maximum Power Point Tracking) guarantees controlled output and makes it easier to get energy from a solar power system. A battery system as well as wind energy use a PI controller to provide energy management. The PV parameters are displayed by node-based MCU-based IOT systems. The hardware result for this study is implemented by using the NODE MCU WI-FI module as well as MATLAB simulation.

articleTitle: A Client-Server Based Educational Chatbot for Academic Institutions
abstract: The use of Generative AI applications in academia, such as ChatGPT, Bard and Perplexity among others is growing at a rapid pace. With its rise, certain ramifications are being felt in regards to the quality and correctness of knowledge and output of these apps. This is detrimental to the process of learning and understanding subject matter in relevant context. In order to stop this issue in its tracks, a solution must be identified, built, tested and deployed so that students will get reliable outputs from trusted sources. This research analyses and describes a sample architecture as well as implementation for such a solution. It incorporates the latest in AI research and development, such as the Large Language Model Mixture of Experts (MoE) architecture as well as a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) with a vector store to use trusted documents such as presentation files, PDF handouts and more from instructors. This is used to add context to the request to the Large Language Model and enrich the understanding as well as response of the model. Apart from this, the application is packaged into a server that can be run on the intranet, as well as deployed for public access. A frontend client page is served to the user, and communicates with the server for all its functioning.

articleTitle: Safeguarding Log Data Integrity: Employing DES Encryption Against Manipulation Attempts
abstract: Log data is a critical asset for security professionals, yet it is vulnerable to misuse and unauthorized access. Attackers often seek to erase or alter incriminating evidence to evade detection. To counter this threat, we employ DES encryption to safeguard log data, ensuring its integrity even in the face of manipulation attempts. Any attempt by an unauthorized user to access trustworthy information triggers safeguards, logging their IP address, date and time of access, source and destination ports, and other relevant details separately. This not only protects against illegal access but also equips law enforcement with vital information to thwart potential attacks. Furthermore, we maintain an intrusion log, documenting unauthorized access attempts for legal purposes. This log serves as valuable evidence in court, aiding in the prosecution of attackers. Our approach effectively mitigates the risk of illegal log manipulation and provides law enforcement with the necessary tools to combat cyber threats.

articleTitle: Enhancing DNS Light Attack Detection through RNN-RF Integration for Imbalanced Data
abstract: In order to maintain the network’s security and ensure that users continue to have faith in it, it is of utmost importance to protect it against DNS lightweight attacks. The application of deep learning is a helpful method that may be utilized to strengthen defense against threats of this nature. Through the utilization of deep learning techniques, networks are able to more effectively detect and eliminate DNS lightweight threats. To prevent anyone from stealing data and gaining access without authorization, these methods search for patterns in DNS traffic to identify inappropriate conduct. Deep learning has the potential to considerably simplify the process of locating and preventing DNS lightweight attacks, which would result in networks that are both more secure and more dependable. Using deep learning to enhance the safety of networks is one approach that may be used to accomplish this goal. With Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) and Random Forest working together, DNS lightweight attacks are much less likely to succeed. This strategy effectively identified and addressed these potential risks by taking into consideration a variety of criteria, including loss, accuracy, val-loss, and valaccuracy. When these technologies are combined, network security improves because DNS traffic trends may be analyzed to detect signals of malicious conduct. When these variables are utilized, the model becomes more robust and better able to detect and prevent DNS lightweight attacks. This improves network security overall. The research effort utilized the Bell-DNS-EXF-2021 dataset to gain a comprehensive understanding of DNS network threats and to devise strategies to mitigate them.

articleTitle: Simulation-Based Evaluation of IDMT Characteristics for Overcurrent Relay Protection
abstract: In the realm of power system protection, the identified problem of reliable protection scheme underscores a crucial void in the design and execution of Inverse Definite Minimum Time (IDMT) overcurrent protection mechanisms. This paper highlights a critical gap in the design and implementation of IDMT overcurrent protection within power systems. Despite advancements in power system protection research and education, there is a lack of a systematic approach to designing and implementing numerical IDMT overcurrent relay characteristics. The absence of standardized methodologies and tools poses challenges to the reliability and effectiveness of protection schemes. The research aims to address this gap by developing and validating IDMT overcurrent relay characteristics following IEC 60255 standards. The objectives include creating a systematic methodology, simulating the designed characteristics using MATLAB/Simulink, and evaluating the performance in terms of speed, selectivity, and reliability. The software implementation involves a detailed Simulink model of an electrical system with an IDMT protection mechanism. The research emphasizes the need for a robust methodology to enhance the understanding and optimization of IDMT overcurrent protection in electrical power systems.

articleTitle: Transforming Sign Language Through Innovations In Machine Vision
abstract: This paper systematically explores the various stages involved in the development of a Sign Language system. To create a system capable of comprehending and interpreting signs, it is essential to train it with an extensive dataset and employ the most effective algorithm available. A fundamental Sign Language Recognition (SLR) system is crafted, focusing on an isolated recognition model. This model relies on vision-based techniques for the detection and recognition of isolated hand gestures. Utilizing a feature extraction and employing Convolution Neural Networks (CNN) for classification, the model achieved an impressive accuracy rate of $\mathbf{9 9 \%}$.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Deep Learning Models for Brain Tumor Classification
abstract: Brain tumor is a fetal disease nowadays that leads to cancer, so detecting brain tumors at an early stage is very crucial. There are many deep neural networks available in the field of medical image processing to detect brain tumors. This paper compares four deep-learning techniques for classifying brain tumor. The models that are used in this model are DenseNet-121, ResNet-50, VGG-16 and Inception-V3. The performance evaluation is based on accuracy, precision, F1-score, AUC ROC score, and Cohen Kappa score on the brain-tumor-detection-mri Dataset from Kaggle. A total of 2400 + images belonging to two classes. We have an accuracy of $\mathbf{9 4. 5 \%}$ for DenseNet-121, 97.5% for ResNet-50, and 94% for VGG-16 and Inception-V3, and we have a score of $73 \%$. The results provide insights into the strengths and weaknesses of each technique and offer guidance for selecting the most suitable approach for image classification in the medical imaging domain.

articleTitle: Speaker Identification Using CNN-LSTM Model on RAVDESS Dataset: A Deep Learning Approach
abstract: Speaker identification is used for identifying an individual based on their voice. Signal processing and deep neural networks are used for feature extraction. This paper presents a method that combines CNN and LSTM for speaker identification. Multiple models such as GMM, CNN, SVM were compared and CNN+LSTM outperformed with an accuracy of 96.52% and F1 measure of 97%. The CNN+LSTM model combines spatial and temporal information extracted by the CNN and LSTM layers which allows to capture of both local and long-term dependencies in the audio data hence making this model very efficient. The above models were evaluated on the RAVDESS (Ryerson AudioVisual Database of Emotional Speech and Song) dataset. The results highlight their potential for practical applications within speaker identification systems.

articleTitle: Dual Zone Air Conditioning and Crash Detection Helmet
abstract: People in various spheres of life including industrial workers and cyclists are more concerned than ever about comfort (they want nothing but the best). However, safety is still the ultimate priority. This article introduces Dual Zone Air Conditioning and Crash Detection Helmet (DACCDH) which combines advanced temperature control technology with an integrated crash detection system. While maintaining optimum levels of security the helmet can provide exceptional comfort to its users. The helmet incorporates dual zone air conditioning functionality whereby it is capable of regulating temperatures within the headgear during winter or summer seasons. DACCDH has a highly sophisticated crash detection system, during accidents or collisions the sensors as well as algorithms works on fast detecting and analyzing impact force on a sudden basis. In case of an accident, sensors trigger an alert that notifies emergency service providers who then rush to save lives by giving medical help promptly. The dual zone air conditioning and crash detection helmet represents a breakthrough in personal protective equipment. Its distinctive blend of comfort, temperature management as well as accident sensing capabilities solves the inadequacies found in conventional helmets guaranteeing maximum user comfort and protection. The helmet is not only designed in a manner that anyone can use it effortlessly but also made light to facilitate easy handling while its low cost makes it affordable even for businesses operating in different sectors. The combination of sophisticated air conditioning technology with crash detection abilities, this state-of-the-art headgear outperforms old-style helmets in terms of effectiveness and ease of use.

articleTitle: Performance and Analysis of Approximate Multipliers using Modified Dual-Stage 5:2 Compressors
abstract: This paper presents a modified approach to approximate multiplier design utilizing dual-stage 5:2 compressors. Multipliers are fundamental components in digital signal processing and computing systems, often demanding a trade-off between accuracy and resource utilization. Approximate computing offers a promising paradigm to mitigate this trade-off by exploiting inherent error resilience in certain applications. Our proposed de-sign leverages dual-stage 5:2 compressors, a specialized architecture optimized for efficient and high-performance multiplication operations. By introducing controlled approximation techniques, we achieve significant improvements in power efficiency and area utilization compared to traditional multiplier designs by 36.37% and 34%. We provide comprehensive simulation results demonstrating the effectiveness of our approach across various benchmarks, highlighting substantial gains in performance while maintaining acceptable levels of accuracy. This work contributes to advancing the state-of-the-art in approximate multiplier design, offering valuable insights for designing energy-efficient and resource-aware computing systems. So that a total of two different 4:2 approximate compressors are analyzed and one 5:2 compressor proposed. The proposed compressors are utilized to implement 8*8 and 16*16 Dadda multiplier. The analysis is further extended to project the application of the implemented design in error resilient applications like image smoothing and image multiplication.

articleTitle: Enhanced Traffic Sign Recognition Using Advanced YOLOv8 Model
abstract: This study proposed an improved traffic sign recognition system based on the latest you only look once version 8 (YOLOv8) architecture. Efficient detection and classification of traffic signs are the keys to preventing traffic accidents and providing traffic management with the necessary control. Real-world traffic scenarios with complex lighting conditions and occlusions are usually where traditional approaches to traffic sign recognition fail to score big. Anticipating these challenges, deep learning techniques have witnessed a growth in popularity due to their enhanced accuracy and resilience in traffic sign recognition tasks. This system is designed to stand on the shoulders of the YOLOv8 model, a known leader in the area of speed and accuracy in object detection. The research focuses on classifying traffic signs into four distinct categories: traffic lights, speed limit signs, stop signs, and crosswalk markings. A dataset consisting of images of traffic signs in all environmental conditions is used for training and testing the model. The method is composed of dataset collection, data preprocessing, model architecture design, training procedure, and evaluation metrics. The accuracy and robustness of the YOLOv8 model in traffic sign recognition are measured by performance metrics like precision, recall, F1-score, and mean average precision (mAP). Comparisons of the developed approach with the state-of-the-art methods allow us to conclude the effectiveness of the approach.

articleTitle: Classification of Cauliflower Leaf Diseases was Accomplished with a High Degree of Accuracy using the CNN-SVM Approach
abstract: In the summary of the research, the findings as well as the metrics of the disease classification model that was constructed for cauliflower leaves are summarized. The model displays outstanding precision, recall, and F1 scores for differentiating the healthy and unhealthy class, unhealthy leaves which are infected from Downy Mildew, Black Rot, Bacterial Leaf Spot, Clubroot, and White Rust. This is accomplished through the utilization of a combination of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Support Vector Machines (SVM). Having precision values for health class 97.32% and 98.38% for unhealthy, the model demonstrates a high level of accuracy in properly recognizing and demonstrating that the model can accurately represent a significant fraction of the actual cases of each condition. The robustness of the model in terms of achieving accurate and dependable classifications is further confirmed by the F1 scores, which represent a harmonious balance between accuracy and recall. 2000 photos were used for training and evaluation. The model was stunningly accurate at 97.52%.

articleTitle: Implementation of Smart Solar Power System Monitoring and Automated Cleaning Mechanism with Python based Embedded Technology
abstract: The research paper focuses on the design and implementation of a 55 Watts solar power monitoring and automated cleaning system integrated with Python-based embedded technology. The system aims to maximize the efficiency of solar power generation by monitoring the output of the solar panel and automatically cleaning it when necessary to maintain optimal performance. The system consists of voltage and current sensors to monitor the solar panel output, a DHT11 sensor to measure temperature and humidity. The LDR sensor is to detect ambient light levels. The data from the sensors are processed by an Arduino Uno board and sent to a Node MCU board which communicates with a server to $\log$ and display the data on the LCD screen. The Python program running on the Node MCU board analyses the sensors and triggers an automatic cleaning mechanism using an L293 driver to move cleaning brush across the surface of the solar panel. This ensures the solar panel remains free from dust and dirt.

articleTitle: Enhanced Drowsiness Prediction through EEG Signal Analysis using Hybrid Machine Learning Model
abstract: The reason for this examination is to give a clever strategy to foreseeing sluggishness by utilizing electroencephalogram (EEG) signal examination related to a mixture AI model. There are a few unique fields where sluggishness identification is vital, including medical services and transportation wellbeing. There is many times an absence of accuracy and strength in customary strategies. With the end goal of this examination, we utilize the broad transient data that is accumulated by EEG signals to plan a drowsiness forecast framework that is more reliable. The methodology that we use integrates approaches for highlight extraction with a cross breed AI model that joins profound learning and conventional AI calculations. In addition to the fact that the half breed model further develops interpretability and speculation, yet it likewise prevails with regards to catching perplexing examples in EEG information. To exhibit the viability of our recommended technique, we completed tests on an EEG dataset that was available to the overall population and gotten empowering discoveries. Because of its unrivaled exhibition as far as exactness and flexibility, the proposed model shows its true capacity for certifiable applications in the space of languor expectation and alleviation.

articleTitle: Navigating Water Scarcity with IoT: A Smart Management System Approach
abstract: A system in place for real-time monitoring, leak detection, water use optimizations, and water distribution that can adjust through IoT technologies dynamically is being developed; it includes high-tech solutions. The prototype design is based on a combination of hardware (sensors and actuators) with software, such as a data management platform and notification system, to develop a water management system characterized by efficiency and flexibility. In water management technology, practical experimentation in the actual environment manifests a higher rate of improvement in water management practices. The outcomes showcased monitoring accuracy at 95%, indicating that system performance can ensure the real-time consumption data is foolproof and dependable. The system proved to be 85% accurate at detecting water half, proving it was an efficient way of quickly resolving water loss. Moreover, the system showed an impressive increase in efficiency up to 90 %. The system is now one of the crucial elements in increasing water utility distribution and conservation efforts. The system also showed its effectiveness through user input (88% of the respondents said they were happy). An indication of the system’s usability and the quality of water management, the overall 80% satisfaction rate suggests. The research assesses how the system performs and its peculiarities compared to current studies, emphasizing its innovation in water systems’ IoT applications. Besides the fact that system issues like compatibility and scalability are provided in the study, the field of research is open for further investigations, such as looking for the role of modern predictive analytics and pursuing user-oriented features.

articleTitle: Hybrid Deep Transfer Learning Framework for Humerus Fracture Detection and Classification from X-ray Images
abstract: The detection and classification of humerus fractures from X-ray images are crucial for effective medical diagnosis and treatment planning. Manual assessment of such fractures is time-consuming and prone to errors, emphasizing the need for automated systems. In this study, we propose a Hybrid Deep Transfer Learning Framework for Humerus Fracture Detection and Classification from X-ray Images. Leveraging deep learning techniques, we amassed a dataset of 1266 radiographic images from the publicly available MURA dataset, encompassing both negative (non-fractured) and positive (fractured) cases. Preprocessing techniques were employed to enhance image quality, followed by data augmentation to mitigate overfitting and bolster system accuracy. Subsequently, a hybrid model comprising ResNet50 and DenseNet121 architectures was utilized for feature extraction and classification. Through experimentation with various optimizers, we achieved the highest accuracy of $93.41 \%$ using the Adam optimizer. Additionally, precision, recall, and F1-score metrics were computed to evaluate model performance comprehensively. Comparative analyses were conducted with other pre-trained models, showcasing the effectiveness of our proposed framework. Our results highlight the deep transfer learning’s effectiveness in humerus fracture detection, providing a promising path forward for the development of medical imaging technologies.

articleTitle: ECG Data Security and Privacy: Leveraging Federated Learning for Better Classification
abstract: The terms of using machine learning and the protection of privacy via the use of federated learning in healthcare, specifically in the case of the ASCO program, have now come to a close. This study focuses on the current deployment of Federated Learning methodologies for classifying ECG information. In this research, we chose the True Active Digital HR Health Record to compare the FML with the one that is IID and non-IID. Instead, attention is focused on CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) as the base design of the problem under consideration, and also through data profiling by checking the performance of the models after 30 epochs. The results disclose that the centralized model yielded an accuracy of 98.39% and a loss of only 5% on the output. On the other hand, fibro learning that was implemented based on the IID data set was oriented 0.03% higher in accuracy with a loss value of 0.04. Its robust privacy protection features and consistent, substantial accuracy are necessary to maintain its operational effectiveness. Yet, the dissimilarities in Non-IID federated learning also affect the outcomes with a relatively low accuracy rate. The final training was well done, its Loss on the last layers being 0.08, leading to an accuracy rate of 87.70%. It is insightful to suggest that their origin is tied to the massive complexity brought about by data divisions among institutions. Therefore, electrocardiogram recognition data protection techniques may be very beneficial. It demonstrates that the mode of operation has an equivalent or even better function than the primary current models. The ability to recognize and remediate the issues embedded in unequal and mixed nature (Non-I-I-D) dataset distributions is an important field to explore and is significant in the future.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Dermoscopy: Unveiling CNN-SVM Synergy in Skin Lesion Detection
abstract: The created algorithm was assessed rigorously, employing numerous performance metrics that were calculated per the categories of skin lesion detection. The precision for each class ranged from 75.00% to 87.85%, indicating that the majority of the model’s positive predictions were events that did indeed occur. To manage Class 5 to be the best in precision compared to other levels. The recall metrics, which means the announced level of the model’s accuracy in searching for all examples from each class, has a performance range of 72.84% to 84.81%, with Class 2 having the greatest recall. The F1-Score, which includes accuracy and recall, corresponds to a percentage that ranges from 73.90% to 83.00%. Further, the study applied various types of averages in order to establish how the model would apply to different classes. The model workout was done on the wise 79.30%, 79.40%, and 79.23% micro-average for accuracy, recall, and F1-score. Results thus attest that an equal performance in all the classes was achieved without the effect of any class imbalance. The weighted mean, giving similar consideration to the occurrence of real cases in each class, generated accuracy, recall, and F1 scores of 79.48%, 79.24%, and 79.24%, respectively, having a small better bent for classes having greater prevalence. Finally, the Micro-average is demonstrated as it is made up of contributions of all classes, and it shows consistent performance across all those Groups, having accuracy, recalling, and F1-Score all equal to 79.24%. As a result of this research, AI skin lesion identification systems are exposed to the application of CNN-SVM models that can perfectly manage medical diagnostics in future, and the shorter the adaptions and the further model simplification, the higher the relevance of performance evaluation options.

articleTitle: Transforming IoT with Federated Multimodal Learning: A Privacy-Centric Approach
abstract: Suppliers face significant challenges when discussing cloud-based health apps, such as implementing highly secure procedures and rigorous privacy safeguards. This applies to the fact that the acceptance of these applications is limited by the need for such quality of service, which is achieved mainly by reducing latency. This work is devoted to tackling these hurdles through the cutting-edge application of edge computing and model-federated learning aspects. Federated learning, a complex and distributed paradigm for machine learning helps perform computations near the data source and overcomes the constraint problem of a distant data source. Integrating the newest edge computing, our system includes an intelligent instrument that is applied to extract clinical data using Clustered Federated Learning (CFL). The value of this framework is evaluated using the performance metrics of two benchmark datasets, one of which represents different kinds of problems that occur in the day-to-day life of people, which concludes the effectiveness and significance of implementing machine learning at the edge in the health care sector The presented results above strongly suggest the fact that CFL promotes this model results in improvement. The performance indicators of the CFL model showed an appraisal boost with the increments in X-ray and Ultrasound datasets by 16% and 11%, respectively, when compared to those trained conventionally. Hence, edge AI through CFL can achieve the same tasks, and the possible scenarios can also be remarkably superior compared to a centralized data system.

articleTitle: Summarizing News: Unleashing the Power of BART, GPT-2, T5, and Pegasus Models in Text Summarization
abstract: In today’s world, with so much information available online, it’s critical to have a method in place for efficiently and rapidly extracting that information. One important NLP activity is text summarizing, which tries to distill lengthy materials into succinct summaries while maintaining important information. The Exercise of extracting the key data from a document or group of linked papers in order to condense them into a shorter version while maintaining the content’s overall meaning. In real, summarizing a text application has a wide scope of practical applications in different domains, enabling users to efficiently process and extract insights from large volumes of textual data can be seen in tools like QuillBot, Movie platform proving gist of the movie, News Aggregation, Legal Document Analysis. The study investigate the performance of models including a comparative analysis of four models GPT-2, T5, BART and PEGASUS, for abstract generation on the widely used CNN_Daily corpus. The system’s performance will be assessed through metrics such as SacreBLEU and ROUGE metrics. The study also analyzes the pros and cons of each model and provide insights into their effectiveness in generating accurate and informative summaries.All things considered, this work advances the area of text summarization by offering a thorough examination of state-of-the-art methods on a difficult dataset.

articleTitle: Forecasting India’s Air Quality: A Machine Learning Approach for Comprehensive Analysis and Prediction
abstract: With rising industrialization, India confronts increasing difficulties in maintaining air quality regulations. This research proposes a comprehensive analysis and prediction framework based on machine learning approaches for assessing and forecasting the Air Quality Index (AQI) in different place of India. This model takes into account a wide variety of pollutant concentrations that are monitored at regular intervals. This approach, which uses historical data from numerous Indian cities, employs a variety of machine learning methods, including k-Neighbour regression, decision tree regressor, linear regression, and random forest regressor, in addition to support vector regressor. Every model had performed well but the Decision Tree Regression and Random forest has performed best achieving RMSE value as 0.0016 and 0.00095 respectivelly whereas R-Squared value as 0.99 for both the model, indicating strong performance and a substantial progress in air quality prediction. The environmental health risks associated with air pollution have been mitigated by the addition of important knowledge.

Author Keywords: Support Vector Regression and Decision Tree Regression

articleTitle: CNN Model for Handwritten Digit Recognition with Improved Accuracy and Performance Using MNIST Dataset
abstract: Handwritten digit identification is an area that requires substantial attention. It is necessary to take into account the differences in handwritten digits’ size, thickness, position, and orientation when identifying them. With the advent of machine learning techniques, handwritten digit recognition is no longer as challenging as it once was. Handwritten numbers of various kinds that may be found in postal codes, addresses, historical archives, and medical records are all handled by the system. General performance across different handwriting styles is ensured by using machine learning algorithms, especially neural networks trained on big datasets. For improved performance and accuracy in the context of handwritten digit recognition, a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model is put forth and assessed in this study. With its sophisticated convolutional layers and optimal settings, our CNN architecture accurately captures some of the complex properties found in handwritten digits using the widely used MNIST dataset. The work not only advances computer vision research but also sheds light on how CNN architectures could be optimized for practical uses that call for accurate digit recognition. It controls the data and intricacies of diverse writing styles. Its versatility accounts for its exceptional digit recognition abilities in any given circumstance.

articleTitle: Expanding the Horizons of Chinese Text Classification with Federated Learning Across Domains
abstract: Federated learning (FL) is a new technology that can correct privacy issues in machine learning by training models on dispersed units. Through applying a hybrid algorithm comprising Federated Learning (FedLearning), Local Batch Normalization (LBN), and Parameter Factorization Weighting (PFW), the article now introduces a Chinese text classifier called the FedBN-PW-CTC Model. This model intends to ensure that accuracy and F1-value substantially improve when solving text categorization problems. Taking into account the local batch normalization, the weighting of the models, and the federated learning with group leaders is the next in line; this approach assumes the priority of a closer consideration of the different elements in Chinese news content and keeping the information secret. We determine the equivalence of the structural characteristics of Siamese networks and PPG signal databases without and with various patients. The model also offers robust grades of precision and accuracy, accompanying its successful scores. The model is superior to the literature in automating text production with a $94 \%$ F1 score, as indicated by the statistical data and the site accuracy of $95 \%$. For Bank A and B, the confidence level is $94 \%$ and $95 \%$, respectively, and the margin of error is $6 \%$ and $5 \%$.Moreover, the p-values for the accuracy and F1 score comparisons were also calculated to be <0.05. Results indicate the highest increase is most likely. Following the test results, the suggested model can be used to solve other similar privacy-sensitive data processing tasks, such as learning Chinese text classification.

articleTitle: A Data-Driven Approach for CO2 Emission Prediction using Dynamic Mode Decomposition
abstract: Greenhouse gas emission is a significant aggravator of global warming. Predicting CO2 emissions holds several advantages crucial for informed decision-making and sustainable resource management. Prediction and control of emissions are thus becoming increasingly important. Carbon emission prediction has been attempted using multiple paradigms. This work aims to employ a data-driven approach to produce highly accurate predictions of carbon emissions. Emission data from over 200 countries is treated as a time series and the Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD) algorithm is used to make predictions. The data-driven nature of the DMD algorithm can capture the underlying dynamics of the time series data and an accurate prediction can be done for the future period. This approach is analyzed and compared with current techniques to identify its benefits.

articleTitle: An Optimized VGGViT model for the Classification and Detection of lung diseases on Chest X-rays using an Optimized - Vision Transformer
abstract: COVID-19 is a worldwide epidemic, and owing to its sudden genetic variations, locating it is a massive task for healthcare experts today. Existing practices of investigating chest X-rays and CT scans necessitate thorough experience and are tedious, implying that it reduces healthcare experts’ countless hours when people’s lives are in danger. This research aims to enhance chest X-ray classification through the comprehensive fine-tuning of the Vision Transformer (ViT) to achieve cutting-edge performance. In the proposed method, the pre-trained VGG-19 model is employed for extracting features, while the classification tasks are handled using an optimized Visual Transformer (ViT). This particular methodology, referred to as VGGViT, has shown remarkable results, with accuracies of 99.16%, a flawless 100% in sensitivity, a mere 0.03% in misclassification rates, 95.23% in precision, 98.99% specificity, and an F1 score of 97.56%.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence assisted Electric Vehicles Fast Charging Station Design using Grid Distribution Network Model
abstract: The electric vehicle charging station is a game-changer that supplants the older kind of charging stations. Our futuristic electric vehicle charging station may be installed virtually anywhere, takes minimal space, and operates independently of the government’s power source, in contrast to the current practice of reserving these stations for major urban areas. Among the many global industries that rely on fossil fuels, transportation ranks high. The development of electric vehicles (EVs) and other forms of transportation electrification are thus essential in the fight against carbon-dioxide emissions and the over-reliance on traditional energy sources that are harmful to the environment. At the same time, electricity distribution, use, and supply have been accompanied by massive amounts of data due to the fast digitization of electrical networks and EVs. These datasets may be used to inform choices and insights by using artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms. Despite a number of recent studies in this area, no one has explicitly examined the usefulness of AI for charge-demand profiling, data augmentation, demand forecasting, explainability of demand, and charge optimization of the EVI. For the purpose of efficiently delivering the fast charging function, this study suggested a novel logic called Grid Distributed Fast EV Charging (GDFEVC). To evaluate the proposed model’s efficiency, it was cross-validated with the standard Fast EV Charging Model (FEVCM). This AI framework has been empirically tested on a real-world EVI case study, and the results show that it helps with the new problems with dispersed energy supplies that are coming up with EV adoption.

articleTitle: DeBERTaSSL: Enhancing Molecular Property Prediction with Self-Supervised Learning
abstract: This research introduces a novel approach to molecular property prediction, leveraging the transformative power of the DeBERTa model, a state-of-the-art transformer-based architecture. By integrating DeBERTa with graph convolutional neural networks (GCNs) and self-supervised learning techniques using fusion modality, our methodology achieves comprehensive representation learning from SMILES-encoded molecular structures. We combine graph-based and sequential representations to capture both local and global relationships within molecules, while incorporating self-supervised learning enables efficient learning from limited labeled data. Through rigorous evaluation and comparison with existing methodologies, including Graph self-supervised learning, Graph Convolutional Network and others, our model DeBERTaSSL, demonstrates superior performance in predicting molecular properties across diverse datasets. This research contributes to advancing the field of molecular property prediction, offering a novel framework that combines the strengths of transformer-based models with graph-based representations and self-supervised learning techniques.

articleTitle: Experimental Evaluation of Secured Forensic Evidence Handling Scheme using Blockchain Technology
abstract: Modern criminal investigations rely on forensic evidence management, which necessitates careful handling, safe storage, and precise documenting of the chain of custody. Problems including data manipulation, illegal access, and a lack of transparency plague conventional evidence management systems. In response to these concerns, this study introduces a novel approach to forensic evidence management that makes use of blockchain technology. Nowadays, data plays a crucial role in every stage of the work process. Since data might change, it should be secure. In a diverse organization, we shall handle data capacity and portrayal. Data that is vital to a particular organization might be the target of an attack. As the prevalence of cybercrime rises, malicious actors are taking increasingly cunning actions to alter such data. Whatever the case may be, it is significantly impacting the expected scientific confirmation of provenance. Since forensic evidence moves through many stages during scientific examination, it is supposed to be preserved in this manner. With this approach, a report is created and then passes through various levels of delegation, such as a pathology lab, a forensic lab, the police, and so on. To create a clear framework with immutable measurable confirmations, blockchain technology innovation is the best choice. The efficiency of the proposed scheme is evaluated by cross-validation with the conventional security model called Secured Forensic Evidence Handler (SFEH). This paper introduced a novel algorithm called Heterogeneous Key Generation for Forensic Data Safety (HKGFDS) to maintain forensic details in a safer manner. By demonstrating how blockchain technology has the ability to revolutionize forensic evidence management methods, this research adds to what is already known. Improved and more trustworthy criminal investigations are possible outcomes of this new line of inquiry and its use in practical forensic contexts. But wider acceptance can’t happen unless scalability and interoperability issues are resolved.

articleTitle: Sarcasm Detection in Newspaper Headlines
abstract: In the current age of information saturation, where headlines serve as primary points of engagement, the pervasive use of sarcasm in news headlines poses a challenge for readers’ comprehension, failing to discern sarcasm may lead to misunderstandings, misinformation dissemination, and harm journalistic integrity. This study addresses this critical issue and enhances the credibility of news sources by employing various ensemble learning algorithms and deep learning models with different types of word embedding, the evaluation includes various possible performance metrics and a complete correlation of the outcomes. XGBoost consistently outperforms other models with higher accuracy, precision, recall, and $F 1$-score in sarcasm detection. Among deep learning models, BiLSTM emerges as the top performer, achieving 0.86 accuracy, capturing nuanced language cues effectively and appears as the optimal model for sarcasm detection. BERT stands out with superior F1 scores, showcasing its exceptional ability in deciphering sarcastic language nuances.

articleTitle: Credit Scoring for Loan Applicants Using Machine Learning Models
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive framework for credit scoring in loan application processes. The research presents a framework that uses data analysis and machine learning techniques to evaluate creditworthiness, in loan applications. By incorporating cutting-edge algorithms like Naive Bayes, SVM, Decision Tree, Multi Layer Perceptron (MLP), and Gradient Booster (GB) the goal is to revolutionize the decision-making process for loan approvals by using analytics. The model utilizes a dataset that includes payment statements enabling a thorough and randomized credit scoring system for each individual applying for a loan. By leveraging machine learning algorithms, the system examines past payment behaviors to extract patterns and information. These findings are then used to generate a credit score that is further classified as good, bad, or moderate. This approach provides an assessment of an applicant’s reliability. To improve the model’s accuracy, feature selection techniques and Synthetic Minority Oversampling Techniques (SMOTE) are utilized to compare models’ effectiveness, in predicting creditworthiness. The integration of data and machine learning not only enhances the efficiency of loan approval processes but also facilitates more informed financial decisions based on data analysis. On all the machine learning models which were performed, SVM performed best among the five models with an F-measure value of 0.86 incorporating feature selection and SMOTE.

articleTitle: An Improved 24μA ±0.5148% High-Precision Bandgap Current Reference integrated with 24mV Voltage Reference
abstract: Thispaper examines the development of a current reference system engineered to generate a constant output current, irrespective of temperature fluctuations, power supply variations, and process deviations. Termed as a ‘Bandgap reference source’ (BGR), the circuit derives its name from its ability to imitate the bandgap energy of silicon semiconductor material, mainly at room temperature. The paper explores theoretical concepts, design considerations, and practical implementations of this bandgap current reference. The system integrates high-precision compensation circuits and nonlinear temperature compensation techniques to achieve a reference current theoretically independent of temperature variations. Through analysis and simulations, the paper establishes the system’s ability to recover to environmental and operational changes, showing its applicability in different settings where precision and stability in current references are essential. The current reference system consistently delivers an output of $24 \mu \mathrm{A}$ with supply voltage of 3.3 V. It possesses a temperature coefficient of $29.401 \mathrm{ppm} /{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, resulting in a current fluctuation of 124 nA.

articleTitle: Advancing Healthcare Accessibility: Development of an AI-Driven Multimodal Chatbot
abstract: In today’s rapidly evolving healthcare sector, the need for efficient and accessible medical assistance is more crucial than ever. With the advancements in Artificial intelligence (AI), healthcare chatbots have emerged as a promising solution to address this need. These chatbots are capable of providing personalized medical information, scheduling appointments, and offering support to patients, thereby enhancing healthcare accessibility and patient engagement. The purpose of this project is to develop an advanced AI-powered healthcare chatbot that builds upon existing technologies to bring significant improvements in patient interaction and healthcare delivery. By leveraging the capabilities of Natural Language Processing (NLP) algorithms and deep learning techniques, the project aims to enhance the chatbot’s functionality by integrating multimodal interaction features, enabling users to interact via text, voice, etc and provide more accurate and relevant responses to user queries. Additionally, the project seeks to create a comprehensive patient portal where users can securely access their medical records, reports, appointments, and engage with the chatbot for personalized assistance.

articleTitle: Securing Cloud-based Data Sharing with Accountable Proxy Re-Encryption
abstract: Cloud computing has been a considerable way to store and share data among different communities in the past few decades. However, it has always been a challenge to ensure that the data is secured during cloud data transfer. The proposed paper resolves the major challenges being faced in cloud data sharing with the new approach of Accountable Proxy-ReEncryption (APRE). The proposed paper deals with protocols and anticipates cryptography measures, namely homomorphic encryption, by ensuring two things: confidentiality and integrity. Both work on the shared data of the cloud. The major aspect of homomorphic encryption is that it has an inbuilt feature of function execution over the encrypted data without decryption. So, it communicates the data confidentially by maintenance. Thus, re-encryption of the proxy used in this research would also allow for safe delegation to the proxy servers. The APRE protocol brings about different accountability mechanisms. In this case, it deals with the aspect of transparency and data supervision in communication. The homomorphic signatures in the paper enable the data owner to monitor and audit the proxy functions. It strictly enforces the decryption policies and minimizes the rate of mishandling of shared information. In so doing, this layer boosts the trust of cloud data sharing, especially in terms of provision of confidentiality, preservation of privacy, and the allowance of the robustness of behaviour in verifying and tracking data access. Finally, this proposed system uses a comprehensive assessment framework to check the effectiveness and efficiency of the APRE protocol. It can, therefore, be inferred that from the outcome obtained from the results, this proposed system outperforms the other existing systems in security, performance, and effectiveness.

articleTitle: Swarm Intelligence Based Feature Selection and Machine Learning Methods for Future Railway Traffic Prediction
abstract: An essential prerequisite for proactive and anticipatory real-time regulation of railroad traffic is the accurate forecast of train delays, or deviations from the schedule. To manage the viability of timetable realization, traffic controllers must forecast the trains’ arrival times in (or approaching) their region. Rescheduled travel, traffic control, data on passengers, and effective route design all rely upon the ability to predict train locations in both space and time in real time. The study introduces a data mining system designed to forecast train traffic. The system utilizes a dataset that includes the scheduled times of all trains and the relationships between them, along with weather characteristics. In order to improve the system’s accuracy in predicting future traffic, research was proposed that would use Swarm Intelligence-based feature selection techniques as Harris Hawk Optimization (HHO). To ascertain the best predictive models in terms of predictive capability, machine learning techniques namely Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) with entity embedding are utilized. It has been demonstrated that the suggested algorithm for processing and analyzing rail traffic is more efficient than alternative approaches and has shown an accuracy rate of 92.3% and precision of 93%.

articleTitle: A Scalable Model for Text Mining using Sentiment Analysis on PySpark
abstract: Sentiment analysis, an essential tool for deciphering public sentiment from vast internet data, offers valuable insights to businesses and policymakers. Its adoption is driven by the ability to interpret emotions, providing guidance for product refinement and decision-making. This tool is crucial for understanding user sentiments, empowering businesses to improve customer experiences, shape brand perception, and refine marketing strategies. Organizations benefit from sentiment analysis by leveraging customer insights for informed decision-making and product enhancement, thereby safeguarding positive relationships and brand reputation. The proposed system utilizes both formal and informal datasets and works on models like Logistic Regression, Naive bayes and SVM. Additionally, feature extraction techniques such as hashing and TF-IDF enhance data representation, contributing to the accuracy and F1-score of the employed models. The proposed system makes use of the PySpark platform to elevate the efficiency.Among the three models utilized, SVM achieved the highest accuracy and F1-score for the Twitter dataset, with an accuracy of 0.76 and an F1-score of 0.76. Similarly, for the Amazon dataset, Logistic Regression exhibited the highest accuracy and F1-score, recording values of 0.89 for both metrics. For comparison and experimental evaluation, the models were executed on a merged dataset comprising both Twitter and Amazon data. In this merged dataset, Logistic Regression outperformed the other models, achieving an accuracy and F1-score of 0.83 for both metrics.

articleTitle: Author Identity Unveiled: Gender and Age Prediction from Textual Patterns using BERT
abstract: The research delves into author profiling, aiming to identify writers’ age groups and genders using extensive textual data. This involves utilizing BERT embeddings to understand sentence structure, word selection, and the overall tone of the writing. The primary goal is to employ supervised machine learning models to categorize authors based on age and gender, aiding marketers in tailoring campaigns for diverse demographics. As for text vectorization methods, BERT embeddings stand out for their ability to capture contextual information efficiently. The objective of this research is to develop a robust solution for author profiling. Additionally, techniques like TF-IDF is also considered effective for text representation, each offering unique advantages depending on the specific task and dataset characteristics. The outcome of this study strongly indicates that the AdaBoost with TF-IDF stands out as the most precise machine learning models for age group prediction with an F1 score of 0.58. The K-neighbours with TF-IDF is the best model for gender prediction with an F1 score of 0.58.

articleTitle: Predictive Modeling with Feature Engineering and Outlier Detection on Airbnb Dataset
abstract: In the burgeoning sector of short-term accommodation, Airbnb stands as a beacon of innovation, reshaping the way travelers experience the world. Yet, with its exponential growth, the quest for optimal pricing remains paramount. This study primarily focuses on the optimization of predictive modelling for Airbnb prices through comprehensive feature engineering and preprocessing techniques. Leveraging a dataset comprising of data acquired from ten major European cities, an in-depth analysis was conducted to improve the accuracy of regression models. Significant enhancements were achieved in the model performance by implementing outlier detection and removal using Z-score approach, feature selection using Variance Threshold (numerical) and Chi-square test (categorical). Linear and Polynomial Regression, Random Forest, Decision Tree, Gradient Boosting and Ensemble Learning (Stacking) models were used for predictive modelling. These findings emphasize and prove the importance of spatial econometric factors in predicting Airbnb prices.

articleTitle: Use of Machine Learning in Object Detection for Visually Impaired Person
abstract: Thisreport presents an object detection model for visually impaired persons for object detection, face recognition, navigation and distance measurement. The system model uses a webcam to captures visual images. The images are compressed to a resolution of 300×300 pixels. The MobilenetV3 model is used for object detection which then are classified into human and non-human types. A face detection algorithm is used to recognize human faces. The distance measurement process uses the focal length of the camera and a calibration pattern to calculate the distance of the objects. The proposed object detection model achieved an impressive performance on the test dataset with an average precision of 92.5%, achieving an accuracy of more than 98% for human detection and approximately 91.7% for other objects. The proposed integrated model’s high accuracy and precision make it a promising solution for the visually impaired people

articleTitle: Ensuring Confidentiality: A Secure Deduplication Model to Prevent Healthcare Records over Cloud Computing Environment with Advanced Crypto Logics
abstract: The exponential growth of electronic health records (EHRs) in healthcare systems necessitates innovative strategies for safeguarding patient data, especially in scenarios involving contentious information. In response to this imperative, we introduce a groundbreaking data deduplication-based encryption framework tailored to ensure semantic protection within Healthcare Records. This framework not only fortifies the confidentiality and integrity of sensitive healthcare data but also enhances the overall cryptographic system for shared information. Our proposed methodology leverages semantically protected encryption, employing a symmetric outer approach fortified by the Modified Quantum Key Distribution (MQKD) algorithm. Unlike conventional cryptographic techniques such as Diffie-Hellman (DH), Advanced Encryption Standard (AES), and Rivest-Shamir-Adleman (RSA), our framework introduces a novel dimension by incorporating MQKD. This integration enhances the Compression Factor, surpassing the performance of traditional methods, and thereby elevating the security posture of the entire system. The synergistic combination of data deduplication and semantically protected encryption addresses the unique challenges posed by contentious healthcare data. By implementing this framework, healthcare providers can ensure not only the confidentiality of patient records but also streamline the secure sharing of information across authorized entities. Our contribution not only responds to the current demand for robust healthcare data security but also opens avenues for further exploration of advanced cryptographic techniques in the healthcare domain.

articleTitle: Towards Automated Lip Reading: Developing Marathi Lip Reading Datasets and Neural Network Frameworks
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative method for automating lip-reading, with a specific focus on the Marathi language. Lip-reading plays a crucial role in aiding those with hearing impairments, but automating it presents significant challenges, especially for languages like Marathi lacking sufficient datasets. To tackle this, we propose a novel approach to automatic lip-reading, accompanied by the development of a specialized Marathi dataset. Leveraging advancements in computer vision and deep learning, our model deciphers linguistic content from lip movements, trained on this dataset. We employ various neural network architectures, including feed-forward, recurrent, and convolutional networks, to extract vital visual features crucial for accurate language interpretation Our primary goal is to provide a robust solution for automated lip-reading tailored specifically to regional languages like Marathi, aiming to enhance accessibility for individuals with hearing impairments, particularly in linguistically diverse contexts. This paper primarily discusses detailed exploration of dataset creation, neural network architectures for lip-reading system, we demonstrate the feasibility and potential impact of our approach. Our study underscores the significance of giving priority to regional languages in technological advancements to promote inclusivity for all individuals.

articleTitle: Improving the Prediction and Fine-Grained Approach for Predicting and Forecasting Cryptocurrency Price Using ARIMA
abstract: A capacity of foreseeing price fluctuations in bitcoin with exceptionally precise is very worthwhile to investigators and funding sources. However, as the cryptocurrency market is nonlinear, it can be challenging to determine the distinctive features of time-series data, which renders it challenging to forecast accurate price estimations. Massive oscillations in non-stationary cryptocurrency values underscore the pressing necessity to precise forecasting models. The most effective methodology for cryptocurrency price forecasting is machine learning, foremost ensemble and deep learning. Traditional statistical methods are difficult to execute accurately because to the lack of seasonal variations and the need to meet a number of naive requirements. The suggested methodology builds upon the random walk theory, commonly utilized in financial markets to model stock values. To simulate market volatility, this methodology utilizes randomization into the observed feature activations of neural networks at a layer-wise level. Moreover, a mechanism to assess the market’s reaction pattern is incorporated into the prediction model. Training was conducted on ARIMA and LSTM, short for Long Short-Term Memory models using Ripple, Ethereum, and Tron as illustrative examples.

articleTitle: MMSD-CAF: MultiModal Sarcasm Detection using CoAttention and Fusion Mechanisms
abstract: A lot of posts and comments across social media platforms including but not limited to Twitter, Instagram intend sarcasm. Sarcasm is a figurative language not just reliant on the text but also on various contextual cues. In our work herewith, we leverage the usage of multimodal cues in the form of textual and image data. The goal is to capture the relationship of sarcasm between the two modalities through deep learning techniques. We evolve our model over three iterations using different embedding representations for text and images while utilising different fusions of text embeddings from FLAVA text encoder and BERT model while image embeddings from FLAVA image encoder and VGG19 model. We leverage mechanisms of co-attention, multi-head attention and keyless attention to capture the contextual cues. Moreover, we utilise the publicly available MMSD2.0 dataset all across. The results are evaluated on the test data in terms of accuracy, precision, recall and F1-score. In the following paper, we show that our proposed novel model, hence named MMSD-CAF, using FLAVA text, image and multimodal learned embeddings along with co-attention and keyless attention-based fusion is able to produce better results than the established models.

articleTitle: Security Analysis of Two Authentication and Key Agreement Protocols Based on Multi-Server Architecture
abstract: This paper delves into the critical security and privacy challenges associated with the integration of Multi-Server architecture with IoT devices to enhance authentication solutions. Our focus revolves around the examination of protocols proposed by Kumar and Om [1] and Haq et al. [3]. Through an in-depth cryptanalysis of these schemes, we uncover vulnerabilities and limitations, elucidating their susceptibility to various security failures. Kumar and Om’s scheme is revealed to be susceptible to issues such as incorrect login features, vulnerability to traceability attacks, and a lack of forward secrecy, along with the potential leakage of temporary information. In the case of Haq et al.’s scheme, identified weaknesses include compromises in user privacy and susceptibility to key compromise impersonation attacks. The paper underscores the paramount importance of mutual authentication between users and application servers, coupled with the negotiation of session keys to thwart key compromise impersonation attacks. In light of these findings, the paper advocates for the development of a novel, efficient, and secure multi-server authenticated key agreement scheme. Such a scheme should not only address existing security concerns but also be adaptable to diverse environments, including multi-application server scenarios and practical applications such as the Internet of Things, medical IoT, and smart homes.

articleTitle: Design of an Efficient Model for Enhanced Liver and Tumor Segmentation Using Advanced Deep Learning Techniques
abstract: The rapidly evolving landscape of medical imaging necessitates innovative approaches to enhance diagnostic accuracy, particularly in liver and tumor segmentation. Current methodologies often grapple with limitations such as the need for extensive labeled datasets and the challenge of generalizing across diverse pathological presentations. Addressing these constraints, this study introduces a novel deep learning model that amalgamates the prowess of $\mathrm{U}-\mathrm{Net}$ architecture, Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), and Monte Carlo Dropout techniques, each contributing uniquely to overcome the existing barriers. Predominantly, the traditional segmentation models are hindered by their dependency on large, annotated datasets, which are not only scarce but also labor-intensive to produce. Further, these models frequently struggle to maintain consistent performance across varying imaging conditions, a pivotal requirement in medical diagnostics. To surmount these challenges, our proposed model employs a fine-tuning methodology using a U-Net architecture pre-trained on extensive medical image datasets like NIH Chest X-ray or MIMIC-CXR. This strategy leverages the pre-existing knowledge within the network, significantly enhancing the model’s ability to discern and adapt to the specific characteristics inherent in liver and tumor images & samples. In a parallel vein, the model harnesses the capabilities of GANs for data augmentation, generating synthetic yet realistic medical images. This innovative use of GANs addresses the issue of dataset variability, equipping the model to generalize more effectively across a spectrum of liver and tumor appearances, ultimately bolstering its robustness. This approach is particularly advantageous in handling cases with diverse lighting, angles, or pathological conditions, traditionally a stumbling block for segmentation models. Moreover, the incorporation of Monte Carlo Dropout for uncertainty estimation marks a significant stride in the realm of clinical applicability. This technique yields pixel-wise uncertainty maps, offering invaluable insights into the model’s confidence levels in its predictions. Such transparency is crucial in clinical settings, where understanding the model’s certainty can guide more informed and cautious decision-making, particularly in scenarios where the cost of erroneous segmentation is high for different scenarios. Empirical evaluation of this composite model on Kaggle datasets has demonstrated its superior performance, evidenced by improvements in precision (3.9%), accuracy (4.9%), recall (4.5%), AUC (8.5%), and a reduction in delay (3.5%) compared to existing methods. The culmination of these advancements not only enhances the efficacy of liver and tumor segmentation but also paves the way for broader applications in medical imaging diagnostics.

articleTitle: Automated Welding Defect Recognition through Deep Learning Fusion: CNN and SVM Integration
abstract: The research is briefly summarized in the abstract, which includes metrics and important conclusions from the assessment of the CNN-SVM hybrid model for welding defect classification. The model performs exceptionally well in terms of precision, recall, and F1-score metrics. It routinely outperforms 96% in terms of all defect classes, including Ideal Weld, Cracks, Porosity, Undercut, and Slag Inclusion. These measures demonstrate the model’s strong capability to detect welding flaws, which is an essential component for guaranteeing structural integrity in a range of industrial settings. The model’s good generalization skills are attributed to the support proportions, which show a balanced representation of fault classes within the dataset. The method was able to classify various welding flaws with an amazing overall accuracy of 96.92% by utilizing a dataset of 4,880 pictures. The model’s remarkably high total accuracy of 96.93% demonstrates its dependability. Additionally, the abstract makes use of macro, weighted, and micro averages to demonstrate the proficiency of the model and provide a comprehensive understanding of its performance. A more nuanced evaluation is provided by the weighted average, which considers the support proportions, while the macro average treats all classes equally. The micro average provides a thorough assessment of the model’s overall performance by combining data from all classes. This study represents the significant advancement in automated welding fault identification with a robust system that satisfies the accuracy or dependability criteria of industrial settings. The abstract provides a concise overview of the work, emphasizing the model’s precision, applicability, and potential impact on enhancing welding inspection protocols across diverse industrial contexts.

articleTitle: Machine Learning based Dynamic Resource Allocation in 6G Network
abstract: The 6G network is a new generation of wireless technology that builds on the $\mathbf{5 G}$ network’s advancements. It aims to improve speed, connectivity, and performance, with high data rates and broad frequency bands. It offers higher capacity and lower latency. Dynamic resource allocation in 6G networks will likely heavily leverage machine learning (ML) techniques due to the complexity and scale of these networks. The resource requirements of devices in 6G network are variable in nature. Dynamic resource allocation is crucial in 6G networks, and machine learning algorithms help to manage resource allocation efficiently. By leveraging machine learning techniques in dynamic resource allocation, $\mathbf{6 G}$ networks can achieve higher efficiency, flexibility, and adaptability to meet the diverse requirements of emerging applications and services. A machine learning algorithm used in this paper showed higher resource utilization and success rate than existing methods.

articleTitle: Enhancing Road Safety in Diminished Vision Conditions: A Deep Learning Approach Using Faster MobileNet for Real-time Object Detection
abstract: Despite significant enhancements in car safety technology, traffic accidents still happen, so finding creative ways to reduce the risk is necessary, particularly in situations with poor vision, like fog. This study presents a unique method using deep learning, namely the Faster MobileNet model, to reduce traffic accidents in situations where eyesight is impaired. The suggested solution makes use of a live video feed from the car’s front-mounted camera and Faster MobileNet to identify and highlight things on the driver’s display instantly. To improve image quality, the system incorporates image processing methods such as data augmentation, normalization, and scaling. Convolutional and pooling layers are used in feature extraction, together with a Region Proposal Network (RPN) to find potential object areas. Classifiers are used in object detection to recognize different kinds of objects and give the driver pertinent information. Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS) is incorporated into the implementation as a post-processing step to eliminate duplicate detections and improve the result. By acting as an intelligent helper, the created application greatly increases poor vision drivers’ visibility and promotes a safer driving environment.

Author Keywords: Region Proposal Network (RPN) and Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS)’

articleTitle: Wheat disease recognition: A Multi-Model Analysis with Customized CNN and Transfer Learning enhanced by Explainable AI techniques with LIME and Grad-CAM
abstract: The integration of deep neural learning and machine learning techniques into crop classification introduces an innovative dimension to agricultural progress. Concurrently, an image-based deep neural learning accession is employed to address the recognition and stratification of disease-affected wheat plants. The study’s core intent is to refine methods for diagnosing and categorizing wheat plant diseases, aligning with the broader aim of enhancing agricultural sustainability. The study unveils the potential of deep neural network models, prominently convolutional neural networks (CNNs), renowned for their effectiveness in image analysis tasks. A comprehensive assessment evaluates five distinct CNN models—VGG19, ResNet50, AlexNet, Inception V3, and DenseNet121—using a publicly accessible dataset for agricultural research referred to as the Large Wheat Disease Classification dataset (LWDCD2020) of 3814 wheat leaf images with four classes such as leaf rust, wheat loose smut, crown and root rot, which are fungal diseases and healthy plant images. The evaluation, focused on accuracy, reveals nuanced differences in performance. VGG19 emerges as the frontrunner with an impressive $\mathbf{9 6 \%}$ accuracy, followed closely by ResNet50, AlexNet, Inception V3, and DenseNet121. These nuances offer practitioners valuable insights for selecting optimal solutions. The study’s emphasis on transparency and clarity extends to the realm of explainable AI techniques. Prominent methods, Grad-CAM and LIME, are employed to shed light on the decision-making processes of deep neural networks (DNNs) models. In this context, Grad-CAM excels in providing more accurate and insightful explanations compared to LIME. These findings underscore the potential of deep neural networks (DNNs) in wheat disease classification and prediction. Beyond conventional performance metrics, the study underscores the significance of explainable AI methods in clarifying model predictions.

articleTitle: Improving Clinical Decision-Making: Detection and Classification of Disease like Kidney Stone from CT Kidney Images Using Deep Learning
abstract: Kidney stones are a common medical problem that causes a lot of people to go to the emergency department because they hurt so much and affect the quality of life. The use of several imaging modalities is essential in the diagnosis of kidney stone disease. The in-depth examination and analysis of these images call for the knowledge and experience of experts. When doctors need a helping hand making a diagnosis, they might turn to computer-aided diagnostic (CAD) techniques, which are practical ways. Recent advances in the application of deep learning methods to AI have prompted the authors of this work to suggest using these methods to automatically diagnose kidney stones by analyzing coronal computed tomography images. An evaluation of a deep learning model (DL) trained for classification tasks is provided in this paper. By examining training and validation data, the research determines the model’s efficacy. With a training and validation accuracy of 99% percent, the model excels at accurately classifying data instances. Contributing to a deeper understanding of the model’s capabilities, the study findings pave the path for its potential use in the world of healthy life.

articleTitle: Smart Healthcare in Smart Cities: Leveraging Machine Learning for Disease Detection
abstract: Machine Learning techniques are leveraged by Smart cities for early identification and intervention of critical diseases. Diabetes and heart diseases are the most common diseases and they have adverse impact on one’s health. Early detection of these diseases can severely reduce their impact. We are applying machine learning algorithms such as Logistic Regression, Decision Trees, KNN, Naïve Bayes, SVM and various ensemble learning techniques such as Random Forest, Bagging Meta Estimator, XGBoost, AdaBoost, Gradient Boost, CatBoost for early detection of respected disease. We have done a comparative study between all the algorithms and chosen the best one by assessing the model in terms of accuracy, recall, f1 score, precision and roc_auc score..Our method can determine whether a patient is detected with a heart disease or diabetes based on selected features of the datasets which were obtained from Kaggle. In case of heart disease, Gradient Boost and CatBoost outperform with Gradient Boost having an accuracy of 88.6% and precision of 88.5% while CatBoost having an accuracy of 89.1% and precision of 89.2%. In case of Diabetes, KNN performs nearly well with an accuracy of 77.9% and precision of 69.2%.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach to Mitigating Traffic Issues through Advanced Congest Detection and Adaptive Signal Control Using AI
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to mitigating traffic issues through the development of an AI- driven intelligent traffic congestion identificationand signal switching system. The proposed system aims to improve traffic flow and reduce congestion by employing advanced congestion detection techniques and adaptive signal control mechanisms. The system utilizes state-of-the-art AI algorithms, such as machine learning and deep learning, to accurately identify congested areas in real-time. By analyzing various traffic parameters, includingtraffic flow, speed, and density, the system can effectively detect and predict congestion patterns. Once a congested area is identified, the system employs adaptive signal control strategies to optimize traffic signal timings and prioritize the flow of traffic in congested zones. This is achieved by dynamically adjusting signal timings based on the current traffic conditions, such as the number of vehicles waiting at each intersection and the expected delay. The system also integrates historicaltraffic data to further enhance congestion predictionaccuracy and signal switching decisions. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed system in reducing traffic congestion and improving overall traffic performance. The AI-driven intelligent traffic congestion identification and signal switching system presented in this paper offer a promising and innovative solution to address traffic issues.

articleTitle: Early Lung Cancer Detection Using CNN
abstract: This paper presents a unique automated strategy for lung cancer detection that employs Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), addressing the global health concern of early detection for improved treatment effectiveness. The study focuses on preparing a heterogeneous dataset that includes both cancerous and non-cancerous lung pictures rigorously split into training, validation, and test sets. Augmentation techniques including zooming, shearing, flipping, and normalization improve the model’s capacity to identify significant features in the mixed dataset. The CNN architecture built using Keras comprises convolutional, maxpooling, and dropout layers designed to detect detailed patterns within lung images. To avoid overfitting, early halting and model checkpointing procedures are used during training, assuring optimal performance and generalization. The trained CNN model achieves an impressive 95% accuracy on the given dataset, demonstrating its efficiency in detecting lung cancer. This study significantly advances automated lung cancer detection methods by proposing a new mixed dataset technique. The high accuracy gained demonstrates CNNs’ potential to revolutionize lung cancer detection, highlighting the critical significance of deep learning in healthcare applications. This unique methodology shows potential for assisting doctors in early diagnosis, improving patient health outcomes.
